name: Necropolis of Banditaccia, Cerveteri
desc:
(Photos ©C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain, and Raoul Kieffer). The Necropoli della Banditaccia, at Cerveteri (Caere, or Cisra), is one of the most important Etruscan sites. It contains a thousand tombs spread over 45 hectares, only part of which is open to the public. The tombs date from the Villanovan culture (9th century BC) to the 3rd century BC.
The oldest are simple shaft tombs. These were followed by hypogeum, tumuli, and dado (cube) tombs. The most recent tombs feature exterior cippi.
The tomb frescoes are famous, and even more so the sarcophagi of the Spouses type, produced in Caere around 520 BC. Most of the remains are exhibited at the Museo Nazionale Etrusco in Rome or the Museo Nazionale Archeology in Cerveteri. - https://artsupp.com/en/cerveteri/museums/necropoli-della-banditaccia

name: La nécropole de Monterozzi, Tarquinia
desc:
"La Necropoli dei Monterozzi est l’un des sites étrusques majeurs, avec celle de Banditaccia.
Elle contient en effet 6000 tombes creusées dans la roche, dont 200 tombes peintes, avec des fresques exceptionnelles. Seule une zone du site (necropoli del Calvario) se visite. Une partie du mobilier funéraire et des fresques sont exposés au Musée archéologique national de Tarquinia. Pour une carte détaillée de la nécropole, cliquez ici :  http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/mappa.htm

name: Tumulus of Camucia
desc: The Tumulo di Camucia was identified in 1840 by A. François. With a considerable perimeter (200 meters), it contains two tombs. - https://aroundus.com/p/11675354-tumulo-di-camucia

name: Necropolis of Sodo
desc: It includes the "Melone" of Camucia, a tumulus tomb, as well as "melones" 1 (which can be visited) and 2, dating from the 7th to 4th centuries BC. In 2005, on the right side of tumulus 2, a vast Orientalizing necropolis was discovered, with two tomb circles and the foundations of a large building. Nearby is the Tomba di Mezzavia, dating from the late 3rd or early 2nd century BC. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/archeological-area-in-cortona/

name: Necropolises of Casetta and Terrone, Bieda (Blera)
desc: The Casetta and Terrone necropolises (extending from it to the northeast) contain a large number of cube tombs, including the famous "Grotta Pinta." This is a monumental tomb with a large chamber supported by a sculpted central pillar and retaining traces of paint. - https://sentieriperblera.altervista.org/necropoli-rupestri-del-terrone-e-della-casetta/

name: Necropolis of Castel d'Asso
desc: The tombs carved into the tufa rock mostly date from between the 4th and 2nd centuries BC: cube tombs, hypogeums, and sarcophagus tombs. Among the most interesting are the Orioli collective tomb, the Tetnie tomb, the Urinates Salvies tomb, and the Tomba Grande. - https://www.visititaly.com/info/989185-necropoli-di-castel-d-asso-viterbo.aspx

name: Necropolis del Portone or dei Marmini, Volterra
desc: Strangely, the once-important Etruscan city of Volterra has yielded few necropolises. Badia and Ulimeto are notable examples, with the most significant being the Hellenistic necropolis (4th to 1st century BC) of Portone (or dei Marmini), which primarily allows visitors to explore two tombs.

name: Puntone Necropolis, Saturnia
desc: The Necropolis of Puntone consists of about thirty rectangular chamber tombs, some covered by a tumulus (7th-6th century BC), accessible via an open-air path (dromos). - https://www.maremma-tuscany.com/saturnia/necropoli-puntone/

name: Folonia Necropolis, Sovana
desc: The necropolis extends along the tufa cliff. It includes various types of tombs dating from the Archaic period, including temple tombs such as the Hellenistic Tomba Siena - https://maremmap.org/ITEM/sorano-sovana-necropoli-del-folonia.html#

name: Sopraripa Necropolis, Sovana
desc: Different types of burials from the 7th to the 2nd century BC (chamber tombs, vaulted tombs, tombs carved into the tufa wall, the furthest being the Tomb of the Siren). - https://maremmap.org/ITEM/sorano-sovana-necropoli-di-sovana-secondo-settore.html

name: Necropolis of Vetulonia
desc: Among the most extensive known necropolises, that of Vetulonia extends across the eastern and western slopes of a hill. It contains the Belvedere Tomb, the Pietrera Tumulus, the Diavolino Tumulus, the Tomb of the Golden Fibula, and nearby, two tomb circles: the Duce Tomb and the Lictor's Tomb (Tomba del Littore) - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/archaeological-area-of-vetulonia/

name: Necropolis of Magliano - Cancellone I – II
desc:
The territory of Magliano has several necropolises with hypogeum tombs, which likely corresponded to small, scattered rural settlements in the 7th-6th centuries BC, abandoned in the 5th century in favor of fortified towns like Doganella. The tombs carved into the limestone include a square chamber with burial benches, sometimes adorned with splendid frescoes (such as the tomb of San Andrea).
Cancellone I: 6th-century tombs with a chamber divided into two parts.
Cancellone II: Tomb E (7th-6th century), more elaborate with side cells and a large chamber, undoubtedly belonged to an aristocratic family. - https://www.maremma-tuscany.com/magliano-in-toscana/etruscans-and-necropolises-in-magliano-in-toscana/

name: Necropolis of Poggio Buco, Pitigliano
desc: The necropolis of Poggio Buco (Statonia, Manciano) spans a long period, from simple pits dug into the tufa, now difficult to access (8th century BC), to chamber tombs entirely carved from tufa (8th century BC), and later, larger tombs. The grave goods consist of ceramics, some of which are exhibited in major museums. - https://www.visititaly.com/info/989154-necropoli-di-poggio-buco-pitigliano.aspx

name: Necropolis of Poggio Tondo, Pian d’Alma
desc: The Poggio Tondo necropolis includes four tombs from the 7th-6th century BC, three of which have a long corridor leading to a rectangular chamber with a dome made of concentric stone rings. A cylindrical tomb and a mound surmounted by a cippus are also present. One tomb contained a chariot, the metal parts of whose wheels have been recovered. - https://www.museidimaremma.it/en/monuments-and-places/etruscan-necropolis-of-poggio-tondo/

name: Necropolis of the Tufa Crucifix , Orvieto
desc: The 70 tombs of the Necropolis of Crocifisso del Tufo (8th-3rd century BC) are buried underground. They are often family tombs, small in size, and their vaults are covered with earth. Funerary benches are found at the walls. - https://artsupp.com/en/orvieto/museums/necropoli-etrusca-di-crocifisso-del-tufo

name: Buche de la Fate Necropolis, Populonia
desc: Hellenistic (3rd-1st century BC) chamber tombs, dug into the rock.

name: Necropolis of Poggio della Porcareccia
desc: Note: see the San Cerbone necropolis, a few meters to the east.

name: Necropolises of Norchia, Vetralla
desc:
(Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). Archaic and Hellenistic tombs, notably from the 4th-2nd centuries BC, are distributed along the waterways.
The facade tombs are carved on several levels. in the tufa, as well as connecting staircases. Some have facades with false doors. Dado (cube) tombs and subterranean tombs, containing sarcophagi bearing the image of the deceased, or funerary benches. The funerary furnishings are preserved in the Civic Museum of Viterbo and the Archaeological Museum of Florence. - https://aroundus.com/p/8127836-norchia

name: Necropolis of the Madonna dell’Olivo, Tuscania
desc:
The Madonna dell'Olivo necropolis, used since the Archaic period, consists mainly of Hellenistic tombs (4th-1st century BC). These tombs are carved into the tufa rock face on several levels.
The most famous tomb is the Grotta della Regina. It comprises a network of galleries carved into a natural cave. The tombs contained a large number of sarcophagi decorated in bas-relief, the lids of which bore reclining figures. The abundant grave goods are preserved at the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Tuscania. - http://musei.beniculturali.it/musei?mid=401&nome=necropoli-madonna-dellolivo

name: Necropolis of Pian di Mola, Tuscania
desc: The Pian di Mola Necropolis (7th to 1st century BC) contains tombs from the Orientalizing, Archaic, Classical, and Hellenistic periods. The latter are the most remarkable. They contained terracotta sarcophagi. See also rock-cut tombs (cube-shaped) such as the Tomba a casa con portico (house-shaped tomb with portico). - https://www.italyformovies.com/location/detail/18598/necropolis-of-pian-di-mola-tuscania

name: Peschiera Necropolis, Tuscania
desc: The Peschiera Necropolis was used primarily in the 6th-5th centuries BC and then until the 1st century BC. Most of the tombs are of the one- or multi-chamber type with a funerary bench, beamed ceilings, and sometimes openings. Although located on private land, it is generally accessible. Of particular note is the Tomba del Dado, an archaic cube-shaped tomb, faithfully reproducing the interior and exterior of a 6th-century BC Etruscan house. Its rear section is carved into the rock. A corridor leads to three chambers furnished with burial beds. Its archaeological artifacts are preserved at the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Tuscania. See also the Tomba Dore. - https://www.tusciaturismo.com/necropoli-etrusche/necropoli-della-peschiera/

name: Necropolis of Ara del Tufo, Tuscania
desc: This small necropolis (7th-3rd century BC) contains Archaic tumulus tombs, with traces of the red paint common at the time, and inhumation or cremation tombs from later periods. - https://www.loquis.com/en/loquis/2941472/Necropolis+Ara+del+Tufo

name: Necropolis of Piane di Vaccina, Ladispoli
desc: On a limestone hill near Ladispoli, this vast Etruscan necropolis contains at least 60 tombs dating from the 7th-6th centuries BC, including two large tumulus tombs and numerous chamber tombs with side beds.

name: Necropolis of the Riserva del Ferrone, Tolfa
desc: The necropolis (mainly 7th-5th centuries BC, and up to the 1st century BC) is located on a tufa plateau overlooking the Lenta Valley, one of the main routes to Cerveteri. It contains 50 tombs, some with tumuli and dado (cube) tombs. Overall, it is distinguished by the richness of the tombs and their ornate architecture, such as the Tomb of the Thrones (Tomba dei Troni), 6th century BC. This necropolis is probably linked to the Etruscan village located at Piana di Stigliano. The grave goods found there are on display at the Tolfa Museum. - https://poloculturaletolfa.com/territorio/il-territorio-aspetti-storico-archeologici/la-necropoli-etrusca-della-riserva-del-ferrone/

name: Necropolis of Pian Conserva, Tolfa
desc: It was occupied continuously from the 7th to the 3rd century BC. Some archaic tombs were reused over time. The most interesting area was located on the summit of the tufa plateau, particularly its easternmost point. The concentration of pottery also suggests the existence of settlements. - https://www.etruskey.it/en/itinerary/pian-della-conserva-etruscan-necropolis-and-roman-road/

name: Necropolis of Monte Abatone, Cerveteri
desc: Remains of this necropolis, dating from the 7th century BC and used until the 3rd century BC, include tumuli and tombs carved into the rock, notably the Campana tumulus, whose chamber featured Etruscan frescoes, and the Torlonia tomb. - https://vici.org/vici/23769/?lang=en

name: Necropolis of Sorbo, Cerveteri
desc: The Sorbo necropolis comprises a series of tombs from the Villanovan period and the 7th century BC, but is best known as the site of the famous Regolini-Galassi tomb, found intact in 1836.

name: Necropolis of Cavalupo, Vulci
desc: The necropolis of Cavalupo (in Italian, Mandrione di Cavalupo) comprises Etruscan tombs dating from the 9th to the 2nd century BC, located near Vulci. The tomba dei bronzetti sardi (9th century BC) contained a cinerary urn and very rich grave goods, including jewelry and three small bronze male figures. - https://catalogo.beniculturali.it/detail/ArchaeologicalProperty/1201339541

name: Necropolis dell'Osteria, Vulci
desc: Chamber tombs (8th-6th centuries BC) with open-air vestibules, carved into the tufa, and Hellenistic tombs. The most famous is the Tomb of the Sculpted Ceilings. The Tomb of the Silver Hands yielded the hands of a statue, ceramics, and jewelry. The Tomb of the Painter of the Bearded Sphinx (Tomba del Pittore della Sfinge barbuta) and of the Panathenaea (Tomba della Panatenaica) revealed other objects (National Etruscan Museum at Villa Giulia in Rome, Vulci Museum). A beautiful statue of a winged sphinx was also found, and even an Egyptian seal. The collected objects are kept in the Archaeological Museum of Florence and the Vulci Museum. - https://www.etruschi.name/vulci/necropoli_osteria_it.html

name: Necropolis of the Three Bridges , Nepi
desc: If only one of the three bridges (tre punti) remains, it leads to a small complex of rock-cut tombs with a portico, four columns, and sculpted lintels between two shields carved into the rock. The path continues as a Roman road to the Rio Maggiore. On the other side is another funerary complex called the Tomba della Regina (Queen's Tomb), consisting of two adjoining and parallel chambers of remarkable architecture. - https://www.etruschi.name/cavo_degli_zucchi/necropoli_tre_ponti_it.html

name: Necropolis of Grotta Porcina , Vetralla
desc: The Grotta Porcina necropolis (6th century BC) features a tumulus 28 meters in diameter and 4 meters high. It contains three chambers. Numerous rock-cut tombs are also visible, as well as a temple and a cylindrical altar approximately 6 meters in diameter, which can be considered the oldest known cult theater in Italy. Near the altar is a Hellenistic tomb. Some of the artifacts are preserved in the Viterbo Museum. - https://www.prolocovetralla.it/2020/11/06/necropoli-di-grotta-porcina/

name: Necropolis of the Rio Purgatorio , Falerii Novi
desc: The necropolises (4th-3rd centuries BC) surrounding the urban center are located on the steep slopes overlooking the Rio Purgatorio and at Pradoro: these are hypogea preceded by a dromos with funerary niches in the walls. Some tombs have an entrance with a columned portico or a burial chamber with a central pillar. Along the Rio Purgatorio, a funerary road has also been unearthed with some chambered tombs with niches, and the Colonnete and Celle areas are composed exclusively of chambered tombs along the Rio Purgatorio. - https://www.italyformovies.com/location/detail/16996/necropolis-of-falerii-novi-fabrica-di-roma

name: Necropolis of Pianezze, Grotte di Castro
desc: The Pianezze Necropolis (7th-6th century BC) contains about thirty tombs. It marks the height of Etruscan civilization. It has yielded rich funerary objects now on display at the Civic Museum of Grotte di Castro. - https://www.italyformovies.com/location/detail/16601/etruscan-necropolis-of-pianezze

name: Necropolis of Castro
desc: In the Ischia di Castro region, shaft and chamber tombs have yielded funerary objects and sculptures in volcanic stone, mainly depicting fantastic animals (winged horses and lions, rams, panthers, sphinxes) that guarded the tombs.

name: Sutri Necropolis
desc: (photo ©Raoul Kieffer) Individual tombs carved into the rock on several levels, some richly decorated with chambers, cornices, pediments, and columns, such is this monumental necropolis of 64 tombs visible from the Via Cassia, dating from the 1st century BC, considered one of the most representative examples of Etruscan-Roman tombs. - https://www.loquis.com/en/loquis/180893/Urban+necropolis+of+Sutri

name: Necropolis of Marangone, Civitavecchia
desc: South of Civitavecchia, near the Marangone stream, was an Etruscan settlement larger than that of Scaglia. The settlement occupied the summit of the Castellina hill. Remnants of the enclosure, totaling 700 meters in length, and sections of road to the east and west remain. The necropolis extends in all directions over approximately 200 hectares. It consists mostly of tumulus tombs surrounded by vertical slabs, with a dromos providing access to the chamber, now often destroyed. The diameter varies from 8 to 10 meters. - https://www.civitavecchia.com/luoghi-siti_archeologici.html

name: Necropolis of Saglia, Civitavecchia
desc: At kilometer 77 of the Via Aurelia, several chamber tombs (6th-5th centuries BC) are visible in a fenced area. Recently restored, they have an underground chamber with a gabled or ogival ceiling and funerary benches. A corridor (dromos) leads down to the chamber. - https://lovecivitavecchia.it/en/punto-interesse/the-scaglia-necropolis/

name: Etruscan Necropolis of Poggino, Castellina in Chianti
desc: The Etruscan necropolis of Poggino near Fonterutoli was used from the 7th to the 5th centuries BC. Five tombs are recorded there. - https://www.visitchianti.net/necropolis-of-poggino/?lang=en

name: Casone Necropolis, Piana del Casone, Val d'Elsa
desc: In this necropolis, used since the 7th century BC, the tomb of Calisna Sepu was discovered, and its excavations formed the core of the museum's collection. - https://eco.museisenesi.org/archivio/1358/necropoli-del-casone/

name: Palazzone Necropolis, Ponte San Giovanni
desc: Another group of Etruscan tombs is located near Perugia. It comprises approximately 200 chamber tombs dug into the ground, mostly Hellenistic. Some are archaic, including five hypogea (Cafat, Acsi, etc.) probably dating from the 6th-5th centuries BC. - https://www.keytoumbria.com/Perugia/Palazzone_Necropolis.html

name: Necropolis of San Cerbone and Casone, Populonia
desc: (photo ©C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain). The necropolises of San Cerbone (southern part) and Casone (northern part) and, next to it, that of Poggio della Porcareccia, date mainly from the Orientalizing and Archaic periods. They contain tumulus tombs of aristocratic families from the 7th century BC, consisting of a cylindrical body on a circular base, temple-shaped tombs (a edicola) from the 6th century BC, and individual cist graves (a cassone) or sarcophagi, from the end of the 6th century BC. - https://tour.parchivaldicornia.app/en/areas/parco-archeologico-di-baratti-e-populonia/necropoli-di-san-cerbone/

name: Necropolis delle Grotte, Populonia
desc: The Necropolis of the Caves (4th-2nd century BC) mainly consists of chamber tombs (hypogea), others with cist graves (sarcophagi), or simple pit graves. - https://archeologiaepaesaggio.it/musei/siti-archeologici/1062-oltre-la-morte-la-necropoli-delle-grotte-a-populonia.html

name: Necropolis of Poggio Granate, Populonia
desc: Outside the park, one can find older necropolises (Poggio del Molino, Poggio delle Granate, Piano delle Granate, from the Villanovan period) as well as those from the Hellenistic period (Poggio Malassarto, New Tombs of Piano delle Granate).

name: Via del ferro necropolis, Populonia
desc: Along the "iron road" that ran from the ore-rich island of Elba to the Adriatic coast, one finds here the remains of ancient blacksmith workshops and several tombs very close by: tomba dei Flabelli, tomba delle Oreficerie, tomba dell'Ayballos, tomba della Spirale d'oro, tomba dei Frammenti Italo-corinzi.

name: Cannicella Necropolis, Orvieto
desc: The Cannicella necropolis (7th-6th century BC) yielded numerous ceramics as well as the Venus of Cannicella, an 80 cm high Parian marble statue (Faina Museum, Orvieto). A temple also stood on the site. - https://www.orvietoviva.com/en/santuario-e-necropoli-della-cannicella/

name: Necropolis of Vigna la Piazza, Grotte di Castro
desc: The necropolis was used for over two centuries (late 8th-early 5th century BC). It contains individual tombs (pit graves or sarcophagi), as well as family tombs with several chambers carved into the tufa. - https://www.archeoares.it/musei/grotte-di-castro/necropoli-di-pianezze-e-centocamere/

name: Necropolis of Santa Maria in Borraccia, Magliano
desc: Tombs (7th-6th century BC) comprising a burial chamber carved into the rock with an access corridor and benches. The entrance is surmounted by an arch and closed by a stone door. The funerary objects are on display at the Archaeological and Art Museum of the Maremma in Grosseto.

name: Necropolis of the Acqua Alta River, Norchia
desc: There are also beautiful temple tombs, two of which feature sculpted Doric facades (3rd century BC). On the left pediment is a group of warriors, on the right three figures, and at the intersection of the tombs, a funeral procession and a winged demon. - https://www.arstum.it/percorsi/luoghi/norchia/

name: Necropolis of the Pile River , Norchia
desc: The most prominent necropolis, with its tufa tombs, includes the Tomb of the Three Heads, the Tomb of Charon, and the Prostila, Ciarlanti, Smurinas, and Germina tombs (with a chimney). - https://www.locchiodihorus.it/2020/11/24/la-necropoli-rupestre-di-pile-a-norchia-vt/

name: Necropolis of Pian del Vescovo
desc: A typical rock-cut necropolis, composed of cube and chamber tombs. Note the Sphinx tomb, named after the sculpted animal. - - https://www.etruskey.it/en/attractions/necropolis-of-pian-del-vescovo/

name: Necropolises of Musarna
desc: In addition to this one, there are five other necropolises to the north and east of Musarna. They include pit and chamber tombs (4th-1st century BC), including those belonging to the Alethnas, and volcanic stone sarcophagi with inscriptions. The recovered objects are housed in the Civic Museum and the National Museum of Rocca Albornoz in Viterbo. - https://catalogo.cultura.gov.it/detail/ArchaeologicalProperty/1201339804

name: Campo della Fiera, Cerveteri
desc: In the southern part of the "fairground" area, this 50-meter-diameter tumulus, the largest in Cerveteri, contains numerous tombs from the 7th-6th centuries BC. The necropolis dates back to the 1st century BC, and it seems it hasn't yet revealed all its secrets… - https://www.campodellafiera.it/

name: Necropolis of Bufolareccia, Cerveteri
desc: This entire necropolis is concentrated on a tufa hill, with a succession of tombs of different types spanning the entire Etruscan period: pit tombs, tumuli, chamber tombs, and shaft tombs. Two funerary paths cross the area, which features small spaces indicating its use as a tufa quarry. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/bufolareccia.htm

name: Valle Trebba Necropolis, Spina
desc: Discovered in the 1920s, and despite leaving few visible traces on the ground, the necropolis revealed 1,300 tombs. Spina, founded in the 6th century BC, was an important emporium (Greek port) on the Adriatic Sea, which became a significant crossroads of trade and civilizations. In total, the necropolises of Valle Trebba and Valle Pega (2 km to the south) have yielded approximately 4,000 tombs, constituting an exceptional heritage, which can be explored in the Ferrara Museum.

name: Necropolis of San Giuliano
desc: (photo ©Raoul Kieffer) The tufa plateau of San Giuliano is entirely within the Marturanum Regional Park. The necropolis consists mainly of archaic tombs (6th-5th centuries BC), but also includes orientalizing tumuli from the 7th century, Hellenistic tombs, cube tombs, hypogeum tombs, pit tombs, etc. Notable examples include the Cuccumella del Caiolo, the Caiolo tumulo, the Tomba dei Letti (Tomb of the Beds), the Portico tomb, the 'Palazzine', the Tomba del Cervo (Tomb of the Stag), the Tomba della Regina (Tomb of the Queen), the Cima tomb, the Rosi tomb, the Costa tomb, the Thansinas tomb, and two tumuli at Valle Cappellana, an archaic group at the locality known as "chiuse Vallerani". - https://www.etruskey.it/en/itinerary/the-necropolis-of-san-giuliano-and-the-park-of-marturanum/

name: Cerracchio Necropolis, Vetralla
desc: The rock-cut necropolis of Cerracchio suggests a modest rural settlement. It expanded during the 6th-5th centuries BC, with interesting small tombs featuring facades with moldings and sculpted doorways. Numerous niche tombs contained cinerary urns, and a few chamber tombs included sarcophagi (4th-3rd centuries BC). - https://www.visititaly.com/info/989187-necropoli-etrusca-del-cerracchio-vetralla.aspx

name: Necropolis of Casa Vignale at San Giovenale, Blera
desc: Next to the Acropolis, traces of dwellings remain, and the necropolis boasts a wide variety of tomb types, from hypogea to subterranean chambers, including Tarquinian-style pointed arches, tumulus tombs, dado (cube) tombs, and semidado tombs.

name: Tombs of Valle Cappellana
desc:
Two interesting tombs lie beneath a large tumulus. Tomb 1, also known as Tomba Margareth (7th-6th century BC), comprises a long dromos, a chamber with a beamed ceiling, and a burial bed. The second chamber contains two columns, very similar to those in the 'Tomb of the Doric Capitals' at Cerveteri.
Tomb 2, known as the 'Tomb of the Throne' (6th century BC), contains two chambers. The first is large and square, with a carved seat near the left-hand bed, similar to those in the 'Chairs and Shields' tomb at Cerveteri. The second chamber has a bench on three sides. A lava stone lion, found on the dromos, is on display at the Barbarano Romano Museum. - https://www.etruskey.it/en/attractions/valle-cappellana-necropolis/

name: Etruscan Necropolis della Certosa, Bologna
desc: The accidental discovery of an Etruscan tomb in the Certosa municipal cemetery initiated a long series of discoveries and the identification of 417 tombs. The hundreds of recovered objects gave a strong impetus to the creation of the Archaeological Museum. The tombs are displayed as they were found during the excavations. - https://www.italia.it/en/emilia-romagna/bologna/monuments/monumental-cemetry-of-the-certosa-di-bologna--main-entrance

name: Moroni-Semprini Necropolis, Verrucchio
desc: Verucchio was a very important Villanovan center, its strategic position allowing control of the entire Marecchia river valley and its port on the sea. Its necropolises have yielded a great deal of material. At the city's height (8th-7th centuries BC), rich tombs of prominent citizens (Moroni-Semprini necropolis) were found, taking on an Etruscan form (chambers carved into the rock, seats, and clothing ornaments). It began to decline at the end of the 7th century BC.

name: Ponte-Rotto necropolis
desc: The necropolis of the Broken Bridge takes its name from the remains of a five-arched bridge that once connected to the city. It is largely abandoned. Here one finds the Bendinelli Tomb, the Mengarelli Tomb, and further north, the Tomb of the Bulls (dei Tori) and the Tomb of the Sarcophagi (dei Sarcofagi). Also present are the Tomb of the Five Chambers (Tomba delle Cinque Camere), found practically intact, the Tomb of the Vestibolo (Tomba del Vestibolo), and the Tomb of the Arcuato Pronaos (Tomba del Pronaos Arcuato). The Tomb of the Two (or Two) is also located here. The Ingressi (of the two entrances), which belonged to the Tetnie family, and some of whose walls are sculpted. Now collapsed, it contained two superb sarcophagi, now in Boston.

name: Polledrara Necropolis
desc: The Polledrara necropolis primarily contains the Cuccumelletta, the Rotunda, and the Constructed Tomb. Finally, there is the Tomb of Isis (Tomba di Iside, 6th century BC), whose current location is unknown, but which contained Egyptian objects demonstrating trade links (glazed pots with hieroglyphs, statuettes, etc.), now in the British Museum. - https://catalogo.beniculturali.it/detail/ArchaeologicalProperty/1201339542

name: Arenosola Necropolis
desc: Around this site was the Arenosola necropolis (but nothing is open to the public), where excavations have unearthed 104 tombs from the 7th to the 3rd century BC, revealing numerous ceramic objects and vessels, some of which are on display at the Provincial Archaeological Museum of Salerno. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_campania/arenosola.htm#:~:text=La%20necropoli%20dell'Arenosola%20testimonia,Paestum)%20all'etrusca%20Pontecagnano.

name: Necropolis of Palastreto
desc: The necropolis of Palastreto (8th-6th century BC) initially consisted of shaft graves, some of which were double (twinned). Later tombs were lined internally with rock. The shafts were filled in, and the recovered artifacts are now in Florence and Sesto Fiorentino. - https://www.museionline.info/toscana-musei-monumenti/necropoli-di-palastreto

name: Pianacce Necropolis
desc: In the "Necropoli delle Pianacce", 21 tombs were discovered, notably the famous Tomb of the Infernal Quadriga, decorated with frescoes typical of the 4th century BC, and a significant sacred theater space. The 300 objects discovered are on display at the Sarteano Museum. - https://sarteanoliving.it/en/la-necropoli-delle-pianacce/

name: Malignano Archaeological Park
desc: The Etruscan necropolis of Malignano, used from the 5th century BC, revealed chamber and shaft tombs carved into the limestone, where ceramics and some coins from the 3rd-2nd centuries BC were found. - https://www.comune.sovicille.si.it/it/vivere/area-archeologica-malignano-56df28af-817e-4410-bee7-f807df80cc6c

name: Necropolis of Prato Rosello, Artimino
desc: The Prato Rosello Necropolis (8th-4th centuries BC) contains tumulus tombs, including Tomb A with a rectangular chamber, and shaft tomb B (the Warrior's Tomb, Tomba del Guerriero). The chamber of tumulus C is supported by a central column. A bucchero nero incense burner was found there. 200 meters to the southeast lies the Grumaggio tumulus. The artifacts collected are now in the Museo Archeologico di Artimino. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/necropolis-of-prato-rosello/

name: Necropolis of Mattonara, Civitavecchia
desc: The Mattonara necropolis was carved into the sedimentary rock. It contains two pit graves, four shaft graves (one of which contained a biconical urn from the 8th century BC), five chambered graves (7th-6th centuries BC), and one hypogeum (5th century AD).

name: Necropolis of Macchia della Signora, Cerveteri
desc: (No information)

name: Casabianda necropolis (Aléria)
desc: Necropolis of Casabianda (Alalia) - In 565 BC, Phocaeans founded a colony at Alalia/Aleria, whose trade would become linked to the great civilizations of the Mediterranean. The Etruscans were interested in Aleria, as were the Carthaginians. The pre-Roman necropolis contains more than 200 tombs, whose grave goods (Attic, Etruscan, and Italiote vases) are on display at the Jérôme Carcopino Departmental Museum in Aleria. - https://ccj.cnrs.fr/spip.php?article2353

name: Necropolis dell’Infernaccio and tumulo Luzi
desc: The Infernaccio necropolis is one of the main sites of the Orientalizing period (7th century BC) in Tarquinia. Among the ancient burials, the Luzi Tumulus is an imposing princely tomb, still visible on the ground, although the drum that would have encircled its base has not been found. It was built over a Villanovan settlement (9th-8th century BC). Of Orientalizing architecture, preceded by a monumental vestibule and a staircase, the chamber is rectangular with a pointed vault. Against the back wall is a funerary bench. Nearby are other smaller princely tumuli with individual chambers and pointed vaults (the Leoncino Tumulus, about 150 m north of the Luzi tomb; the Infernaccetto Tumulus to the south; and the Zanob Tumulus 100 m away). - https://catalogo.cultura.gov.it/detail/ArchaeologicalProperty/1201339188

name: Torano Necropolis, Borgorose
desc: Tumulus tombs, - http://www.archeologia.beniculturali.it/index.php?it/142/scavi/scaviarcheologici_4e048966cfa3a/108

name: Calvario Necropolis, Tarquinia
desc: (Photo ©C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain). The necropolis is divided into 5 zones: Calvario, Primi Archi, Secondi Archi, Area Scataglini, and Doganaccia. Only the Calvario (Calvary) necropolis is open to the public. Around twenty tombs can usually be visited freely; others are only accessible by guided tour (Tomba delle Pantere, Tomba dei Tori, Tomba degli Auguri, Tomba del Barone, and Fondo Scataglini). For a complete map of the Monterozzi necropolis, click here: http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/mappa.htm

name: Necropolis and city of San Giovenale, Blera
desc: (photos ©Luca Camilloni). Occupied since the Bronze Age, this Etruscan city bears traces of dwellings built with blocks of tufa, from the 8th to the 5th century BC, an acropolis and, in the surrounding area, several necropolises (Grotta Tufarina, Porzarago, Castellina, Montevangone, Pontesilli, Vignale). - http://www.lazioturismo.it/asp/scheda_archeo.asp?id=64

name: Necropolises of Dometaia and Le Ville, Colle di Val d'Elsa
desc: Around twenty tombs have been unearthed since 1974, including five large aristocratic tombs from the 6th century BC, and about fifteen smaller ones (4th-1st century AD), stretched along the ridge. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/archaeological-park-of-dometaia/

name: Tomb of the infernal quadriga, Pianacce
desc: Discovered in 2003 and in excellent condition, the "Tomba della Quadriglia Infernale," based on its painting style and the objects found there, can be dated to the second half of the 6th century BC. J.-C. - https://www.montepiesi.it/tomba_quadriga_infernale.htm

name: Belvedere Temple, Orvieto
desc: The Belvedere Temple (Tempio del Belvedere), the only Etruscan temple in Orvieto, probably dates from the early 5th century BC. It was used until the first decades of the 3rd century BC. The foundation, the entrance staircase, the bases of the four facade columns (pronaos), and some enclosure blocks remain. Fragments are preserved at the Museo Faina. - https://aroundus.com/p/8130641-belvedere-temple

name: Etruscan wall of Bettona
desc: The Bettona Wall, the city's defensive wall, approximately 1000 meters long, is ellipsoidal in shape. The perfectly preserved walls are medieval but rest on a wide base of pre-existing Etruscan walls composed of visible sandstone blocks. - https://www.umbriatourism.it/en/-/the-city-wall-of-bettona

name: Acquarossa (near Viterbo)
desc: On the site of Aquarossa stood an Etruscan city from the Archaic period, located at an important crossroads. The remains extend for a kilometer and include a palace (central courtyard bordered by halls) surrounded by agricultural estates with some dwellings. To the north, several monumental buildings can be seen. The National Etruscan Museum in Viterbo displays the objects discovered on the site, which was abandoned or destroyed at the end of the 4th century BC. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/acquarossa/index.htm

name: The Etruscan pyramid of Bomarzo
desc:
Près de Bomarzo, un énorme rocher de tuf (8 x 16m) a été taillé en forme de tronc de pyramide. Il s’agit en fait d’un autel pyramidal qui fut utilisé vers le 7e siècle av. J.-C.
Le bloc a été soigneusement travaillé pour comporter un escalier de 26 marches menant à deux autels intermédiaires. Il faut encore gravir 9 marches pour atteindre celui du sommet.
On notera aussi des sièges, des rigoles, des niches taillés dans le roc, et aux alentours, des habitations troglodytes. - https://fr.thebrainchamber.com/etruscan-pyramid-of-bomarzo/

name: Etruscan walls in Fiesole
desc: While the theater and baths date from the Roman Imperial period, Etruscan walls from the 4th century BC can be seen in this park. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/ideas/city-walls-florentine-area/

name: Etruscan wall of Perugia
desc: The Mura di Perugia refers to the two concentric city walls of Perugia, the inner wall being of Etruscan origin (4th-3rd century BC), the outer wall medieval. The 3-kilometer-long Etruscan wall was modified by the Romans and the Italians. It is 3 kilometers long and has 6 gates, including the Etruscan Arch (Arch of Augustus) and the Etruscan Porta Marzia, which has survived without major alteration. - http://www.perugiaonline.it/perugia_arcoetrusco.html

name: Etruscan Acropolis, Volterra
desc:
Excavations at the Acropolis have unearthed a 6th-century BC quarter dedicated to religious activities, with associated temples, dwellings, and storehouses.
Two Greek-style cult houses (3rd-2nd century BC) are known as Temples A and B, and include other service buildings and a cistern.
On the western edge, a building contained a brightly colored fresco, now in the Guarnacci Museum along with other objects from the site. - https://volterratur.it/en/poi/the-etruscan-acropolis/

name: The city of Marzabotto
desc: The Etruscan city of Kainua was founded in the 6th century BC on the road connecting Tyrrhenian Etruria and Po Valley Etruria. It covers 25 hectares. Its plan is orthogonal, with a wide north-south avenue and three east-west avenues. Monumental entrances are located to the north and east. The acropolis is situated to the northwest on a plateau overlooking the city. The foundations of a divination temple have been identified, and below it, three buildings and two altars. One of the altars covers a sacred well. To the north are the remains of a large temple dedicated to Tinia. To the northeast of the city lies the Sanctuary of the Fountain. Villas, sewers, and workshops for pottery and metalworking (6th-5th centuries BC) were also found. Two necropolises are located outside the walls (168 tombs to the north and 125 to the east). Some tombs were surmounted by a stone egg. The artifacts are preserved in the Museo Nazionale Etrusco "Pompeo Aria". - https://aroundus.com/p/8122221-marzabotto

name: Archaeological Park of Lake Accesa, Massa Marittima
desc: The archaeological site around Lago dell'Accesa, only partially studied, covers several dozen hectares. Five quarters, each with its own necropolis (7th-6th century BC), are being excavated there, although some pit graves appear to be earlier. Also worth visiting is the Archaeological Museum of Massa Marittima. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/lago-accesa-archeological-park/

name: The Etruscan or Augustus Arch, Perugia
desc: The Etruscan Arch, or "Arch of Augustus," in Perugia, is the most complete and monumental of the Etruscan gateways. Built in the second half of the 3rd century BC, it is surmounted by a semicircular niche and flanked by two trapezoidal towers. An earlier gateway was located approximately 20 meters behind it, which was erected to appear more prestigious. - https://aroundus.com/p/8573141-etruscan-arch

name: Porta Marzia, Perugia
desc: The Porta Marzia is one of the gates in the Etruscan city wall of Perugia (Perugia). Dating from the late 3rd century BC, it was moved 4 meters in 1540 to be incorporated into the new wall. It features a semicircular arch, surmounted by a balustrade of four pillars framing five sculptures (Jupiter, Castor, and Pollux in the center, and horses at either end). - https://www.umbriatourism.it/en/-/porta-marzia-en

name: Temple of Talamonaccio, Talamone
desc: Talamonaccio's strategic location led to its occupation since the Neolithic period. By the 4th century, it included a fortified oppidum and a necropolis. The Etruscan-Italic type temple was built at the end of the century and remained in use even after the Roman conquest. The cella, which housed the statue of the deity, was preceded by a columned portico. On the rear façade was a famous pediment (150 BC) depicting the struggle between Eteocles and Polynices, son of Oedipus, now on display in Orbetello. - https://aroundus.com/p/8130639-temple-of-talamonaccio

name: Archaeological site of Veii (Veio)
desc: Ruins of the Sanctuary of Portonaccio. Foundations of the Temple of Apollo (6th century BC), from which the terracotta statue of the Apollo of Veii, exhibited at the Villa Giulia Museum in Rome, originates. - https://aroundus.com/p/11678543-parco-naturale-di-veio

name: Ponte Sodo, Veii
desc: The Ponte Sodo (Solid Bridge) is actually a 70-meter tunnel that was part of the remarkable hydraulic network of Veii (drainage canals and galleries).

name: Temple of Grasceta dei Cavallari, Monte Piantangelia di Tolfa
desc: The Etruscan-Roman sanctuary of Grasceta dei Cavallari was founded in the 6th century BC and expanded during the Hellenistic period (3rd century BC)." Of the temple, only the foundations remain, on a rectangular plan of 10 x 18m. The cella revealed numerous offerings and objects now displayed in the Tolfa museum.

name: Etruscan wall, Volterra
desc: Remains of the ancient wall - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/porta-allarco-volterra/

name: Site of Vitozza, Sorano
desc: The Vitozza site is the largest troglodytic site in Italy, in the area known as the "Area del Tufo." It has more than 200 caves that were inhabited until the 18th century. The presence of paths cut into the tufa (Via Cava) supports the hypothesis of its Etruscan origin. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/the-cave-settlement-of-vitozza/

name: Falerii Novi
desc: In 241 BC, when the Romans destroyed the city of Falerii, the inhabitants built Falerii Novi a few kilometers away. The remains of the new city are impressive: the city walls extend for 2 km, practically intact with their gates, towers, and walls 17 m high. The Gate of Jupiter (Porta di Giove) is one of the earliest examples of the use of the arch in Etruria. Inside the city, one can see the theater and a fragment of the ancient Via Cimina. The National Etruscan Museum at the Villa Giulia in Rome houses objects from the city and necropolises of Falerii Novi. - https://aroundus.com/p/8151166-falerii-novi

name: Porta Bove, Falerii Novi
desc: The city walls, stretching for 2 km, remain intact, retaining their 17m height and the towers that once punctuated the route. The Gate of the Ox (Porta Bove) is so named because of the presence of a sculpted ox head.

name: Musarna (near Viterbo)
desc: The city was surrounded by a ditch and a defensive wall with two gates. The main street was lined with large buildings. The central square contained two temples, one of which was dedicated to Hercules. Baths, galleries, and wells forming a sewer system have been identified. - https://www.visititaly.com/archaeological-sites/lazio/viterbo.aspx

name: Site of Bisenzio
desc: The Etruscan city of Vensnth, or Vishnth, now Bisenzio, on the shores of Lake Bolsena, was known for its shoe and pottery production. It was conquered by the neighboring city of Vulsinii (Bolsena). The archaeological site has yielded numerous artifacts and Villanovan and Etruscan necropolises.

name: Archaeological excavations of Frascole, Dicomano
desc:
The archaeological site of San Martino at Poggio-Frascole is located in the territory of Dicomano, an area rich in archaeological remains. At Frascole, numerous excavations have unearthed (6th century BC to 1st century AD) the rectangular perimeter of an Etruscan building, the mysterious ""fortress"" of the Velasna family, and a large, unfinished temple.
A well-preserved funerary stele in the Fiesole style (6th century BC), decorated in bas-relief, has also been found. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/archeological-excavations-frascole/

name: The city of Ferento, near Viterbo
desc: The city of Ferento had a turbulent history: an agricultural and metallurgical center from the 7th century BC, it was destroyed at the end of the 6th century. Then, in the following century, the hill of Pianicara was occupied by inhabitants likely expelled from Acquarossa, itself destroyed by Tarquinia. It later became the Roman city of Ferentum, with its amphitheater, theater, baths, etc. Etruscan-Roman remains. - https://viterbo.artecitta.it/en/the-archaeological-area-of-ferento/

name: Excavations of the Greco-Etruscan Emporio of Gravisca
desc: In the 6th century BC, Gravisca was the port of Tarquinia and also a Greek emporium, a port colony with a small sanctuary dedicated to Aphrodite. An object dedicated to the Etruscan goddess Turan shows that the site was also visited by Etruscans. A sanctuary dedicated to Hera (Uni to the Etruscans) has also been discovered. Demeter and Apollo were also honored. At the beginning of the 5th century BC, the Greeks were no longer present, and the sanctuary was enlarged by the Etruscans. The Romans settled on this site and on the Etruscan ruins in 181 BC. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/gravisca/?lang=en

name: Lake of the Idols
desc: More than 2,600 years ago, the Etruscans began throwing offerings and votive offerings into the small Lago degli Idoli (Lake of the Idols), which was drained in 1838 to carry out highly fruitful excavations: more than 600 small bronze statuettes representing human figures and animals were discovered, now exhibited in the largest museums in the world. Museums of the world… Chains, fibulae, coins, more than 2,000 arrowheads, and even some intact vases dating from the 6th century BC to the Hellenistic period were also found. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/lago-degli-idoli/

name: Remains of Poggio Colla, Vicchio
desc: The archaeological site of Poggio Colla reveals remains from the Archaic to the Hellenistic periods. Monumental structures, pottery fragments, and ornaments attest to the site's wealth and its connections with other civilizations. The site includes enclosure walls and a necropolis area. In 2016, a 6th-century stele bearing a 70-character Etruscan inscription was discovered in the foundations of a temple. - https://rethinkingetruria.com/theme/poggio

name: Citadel of Rofalco
desc: In the heart of the Lamone Nature Reserve, Rofalco (an Etruscan site dating from the 4th-3rd centuries BC) rises above the Olpeta River. The fortress controlled an important trade route connecting Orvieto to the sea. Its dry-stone wall, constructed with large polygonal blocks, forms an arc approximately 330 meters long and about 6 meters thick. The preserved height reaches nearly 4 meters in places. Three large towers are still visible. Within the town, a residential area and a building composed of a series of five compartments, likely a warehouse, have been identified. - https://www.etruschi.name/rofalco/index.html

name: Labyrinth of Porsenna, Chiusi
desc: The Labirinto di Porsenna consists of a network of underground galleries for water supply, dug beneath the old town of Chiusi, notably under the cathedral square. It is accessed via the cathedral museum. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/cathedral-museum-and-labyrinth-of-porsenna-in-chiusi/

name: Archaeological Park of Baratti-Populonia, Piombino
desc: This archaeological park, inaugurated in 1998, covers an area of approximately 80 hectares. It contains the acropolis of the Etruscan city of Populonia, the necropolises, and various districts of the city. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/archeological-park-of-baratti-and-populonia/

name: Acropolis of Populonia
desc: The Etruscan Acropolis contains three temples and numerous Etruscan-Roman remains. On the eastern slope, traces of ancient workshops have been found. - https://www.parchivaldicornia.it/en/archaeological-parks/archaeological-park-of-baratti-and-populonia/the-acropolis-of-populonia/

name: Via del Cavone, Sovana
desc: The Vie Cave, also called cavoni (cavone in the singular), are Etruscan thoroughfares sometimes carved 20 meters deep into the tufa rock. - https://vici.org/vici/43489/?lang=en

name: Site of Ghiaccioforte, Scansano
desc: The fortified site of Ghiaccioforte (late 4th century BC) was built on an Archaic rural sanctuary. It defended the territory of Vulci as Roman pressure increased. It was destroyed during the Roman conquest in 280 BC. Traces of the wall and the foundations of dwellings and a workshop remain. - https://www.maremma.it/blog/en/etruscan-archaeological-site-of-ghiaccio-forte/

name: Archaeological site of Roselle
desc: (Photo ©Corinna Pieri) Ancient Rusellae was urbanized from the 7th century BC onwards, and Vetulonia provided it with access to the sea. The wall remains impressive, still standing 5 meters high in some places, and stretching for 3 kilometers. Visitors can explore the remains of a two-room house, a walled building, and a house with one of the oldest known impluviums. An artisan area (6th-4th century BC) and several kilns. Outside the walls, the Serpaio necropolis, at the entrance to the site. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/ideas/roselle-where-ancient-history-brings-to-life/

name: L'Ara della Regina, Tarquinia
desc: The Ara della Regina (Queen's Altar, 4th century BC), on the Pian di Civita hill, displays the remains of a large Etruscan sanctuary with walls and buildings from the ancient city of Tarchuna or Tarchna. The temple, exceptionally large for an Etruscan temple, dates back to the 6th century BC. Its pediment featured a terracotta group, the famous Winged Horses of Tarquinia, now housed in the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/the-sanctuary-of-the-ara-della-regina/?lang=en

name: Greppe di Sant'Angelo
desc: Around the access road (Strada di S. Antonio), there is a high concentration of archaeological sites, some of which are still being studied. These include the ruins of two sanctuaries, one of which was dedicated to Hercules. Halfway up the slope lies the necropolis of Greppe S. Angelo, with the monumental tomb of Charon, featuring a two-tiered façade and a staircase, and two burial chambers. A statue of Charon, two winged sphinxes, and three reclining lions were discovered there. Most of the finds are on display at the Cerite National Museum.

name: The Porta all'Arco, Volterra
desc: The Porta dell'Arco was part of Volterra's city walls in the 3rd-2nd centuries BC. It was little altered by the Romans. It is made of large blocks of tufa. Note the keystone and the two pillars bearing sculpted heads. Other remains of the wall are visible to the north of the city. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/porta-allarco-volterra/

name: Archaeological Park of Forcello di Bagnolo San Vito
desc: The Forcello Archaeological Park in Bagnolo San Vito, near Mantua, is situated on the remains of an important Etruscan settlement dating from the 6th-4th centuries BC, of which a small part has been excavated. The park preserves these remains, disseminates the scientific results of the excavations, and uses them for public outreach and education. - https://www.isprambiente.gov.it/it/attivita/museo/regioni/musei/parco-archeologico-del-forcello

name: Gran Carro, Lago di Bolsena
desc: Beneath the waters of Lake Bolsena lay a Villanovan settlement! Following the rise in water level at the end of the 9th century BC, the dwellings were initially built on stilts (456 have been counted) and eventually abandoned. The funerary remains have provided countless examples of the Villanovan culture: impasto pottery, everyday objects, tools… 4,000 objects have been recovered, exploring only 10% of the area, which covers 77 hectares. - https://visitbolsena.it/en/what-to-do/gran-carro-underwater-archaeological-trail/

name: Remains of Civita d'Arlena
desc: At Civita d'Arlena was located in the 7th-6th centuries BC. In the 1st century BC, a fortified settlement, Turona, was discovered, with a small temple of which only overgrown traces remain. Several necropolises surrounded the hill, the oldest being Villanovan. - https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civita_d%27Arlena

name: Temples of Pyrgi
desc: Remains of ramparts surround the area that contained two temples. Temple A (470-460 BC), of Etruscan type, had three cellae. It has been reconstructed at the National Etruscan Museum in the Villa Giulia. Temple B, built around 510 BC, closer to the Greek temple, has a single cella. It was between the two temples that the Pyrgi tablets were found: three gold sheets bearing Etruscan and Phoenician inscriptions dedicated to the goddess Uni/Astarte. Twenty small, aligned cells suggest the possibility of sacred prostitutes.

name: Vulci Natural and Archaeological Park
desc: Among the most important remains are the walls: the monumental western gate dates from the second half of the 4th century BC. The northern gate has yielded votive offerings (3rd-1st century BC). The city contains several Roman domus, including the Cryptoporticus (criptoportico), a mithraeum, and the foundations of the large temple used from the Archaic to the Roman period. To the east lies the Fiora River, and the river port is still being excavated. On this side, the walls are approximately 4 meters thick. A footbridge provides access to the necropolises. - https://www.italia.it/en/lazio/montalto-di-castro/natural-archaeological-park-of-vulci

name: Etrusco-Samnite archaeological site of Fratte, Salerno
desc:
Excavations at the Etruscan-Samnite archaeological site of Fratte (6th-5th centuries BC), near Salerno, have unearthed a number of tombs and a cistern in the Acropolis area, as well as numerous amphorae containing personal belongings.
The city also had a temple with bas-reliefs. The archaeological finds are on display at the Provincial Archaeological Museum of Salerno. - https://cultura.gov.it/luogo/area-archeologica-di-fratte

name: Site of Luni sul Mignone
desc: Luni sul Mignone is a prehistoric site dating from the Bronze Age and Villanovan period. The cave dwelling, surrounded by Etruscan fortifications made of quadrangular tufa blocks, was abandoned during the Late Etruscan period and reoccupied in the Middle Ages. - https://www.etruskey.it/en/attractions/archaeological-site-of-luni-sul-mignone/

name: Etruscan city of Gonfienti (Camars)
desc: Gonfienti is an ancient Etruscan city from the Archaic period, an important crossroads between Central Etruria and the Po Valley (6th-5th centuries BC). Remains of an Archaic settlement, including several buildings, are found, notably the largest known Etruscan domus, from which numerous artifacts have been recovered. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/archaeological-area-in-gonfienti/

name: The Sant’Omobono area
desc: The site has revealed occupation dating back to the Bronze Age, with numerous successive buildings, including two Etruscan temples: the Temple of Fortuna and the Temple of Mater Matuta, where terracotta statues of Minerva and Hercules (6th century BC) - https://www.turismoroma.it/en/node/1042

name: Sanctuary of the Thirteen Altars, Pomezia
desc: The Santuario delle tredici are consists of a series of travertine altars erected between the 6th and 3rd centuries BC. The offerings deposited there provide information about the rituals practiced and the contacts with the Greek colonies of southern Italy. - https://www.pomeziaetorvajanica.it/torvaianica/da-vedere/area-archeologica-xiii-altari/

name: Galleria di Pietra Pertusa
desc: A spectacular 350m tunnel built by the Etruscans to connect Veii to the Tiber, and then to the sea, passing through the nearby quarries. This saved chariots from having to climb the hill… - https://www.sotterraneidiroma.it/sites/galleria-etrusca-di-pietra-pertusa

name: Regia, forum, Rome
desc: The Regia was originally an official residence of the Etruscan kings of Rome, built under Numa Pompilius. Excavations have identified several layers, dating from the 8th to the 6th centuries BC, followed by reconstructions from the 3rd and 1st centuries BC. A Bucchero cup from the late 6th century BC was found. - https://aroundus.com/p/11673766-regia

name: Sanctuary of Punta della Vipera, Santa Marinella
desc: The temple of Punta della Vipera, built in the 6th century BC, was dedicated to Menrva (Minerva). Restored several times up to the 1st century, then forgotten, only vague vestiges of its enclosure and bothros (a system of channels) remain.

name: Fosso degli Olmetti, La Selvotta
desc: This underground aqueduct is part of an ancient Etruscan water management system, with dams and retention basins. The gallery opens onto a small waterfall. Operating by gravity, it is still in use today. The water supplied the area as far as Veii. - https://www.loquis.com/it/loquis/1505045/Acquedotto+Etrusco+della+Selvotta+Fosso+degli+Olmetti

name: Etruscan altar of Pieve di Socana
desc: (Photo ©Corinna Pieri) For centuries, legend spoke of an important Etruscan place of worship on the site of the current Romanesque parish church of Socana in Casentino. Just a few meters from its apse, excavations have indeed revealed an extraordinary Etruscan altar dating from the 5th century BC. The remains of the associated temple lie beneath the church. Part of its staircase is still visible behind a wire mesh to the left of the apse. - https://www.ilbelcasentino.it/church-socana-en.php

name: La Rotta, Figline Valdarno
desc: Excavations at La Rotta, in Figline Valdarno, have unearthed an important site, occupied from the 8th to the 2nd century BC, revealing remains of dwellings and textile production, as well as pottery (impasto, bucchero, Attic pottery) indicating an aristocratic presence. The excavations are ongoing. A museum is being considered.

name: Etruscan cippus, San Lorenzo Nuovo

name: Ancient city of Vetulonia
