desc: The Tanella of Pythagoras is located on the slope descending from the Cortona hill towards the Chiana valley. It is a small Hellenistic tumulus consisting of a circular base supporting a stone drum. A small rectangular chamber is covered by a vault - https://www.accademia-etrusca.org/tombe-accademia-etrusca/

name: Tomb of Mezzavia, Sodo
desc: Near the Sodo necropolis, the Tomba di Mezzavia dates from the late 3rd or early 2nd century BC.

name: Tanella Angori, Sodo
desc: The Tanella Angori, not far from the Tanella of Pythagoras, also dates from the Hellenistic period (2nd century BC). Only the base and a few blocks of the vault remain.

name: Hypogeum of the Volumni, Ponte San Giovanni
desc: The tomb of the Volumni family, probably from the 3rd-1st century BC, is typical of the Hellenistic Etruscan period. It is part of the vast Palazzone necropolis (6th-5th century BC). It has three central chambers and four small side chambers. - https://aroundus.com/p/11674883-hypogeum-of-the-volumnus-family

name: Tomb of Faggeto, Perugia
desc: The Faggeto tomb (2nd century BC) was carved into the sandstone on a hillside near Mount Tezio, San Giovanni Pantano. A cinerary urn and some funerary objects were found there. Its distinctive feature is the presence of a closing door. - https://www.umbriatourism.it/fr/-/tomba-del-faggeto-fr

name: Etruscan hypogeum of Bettona
desc: The hypogeum, near Bettona, dates from the 3rd-2nd century BC. The burial chamber, dating from the 5th century BC, is constructed of large stone blocks and covered by a barrel vault. An open-air corridor leads to the entrance. The funerary furnishings are preserved in the Etruscan Museum of Perugia and the Archaeological Museum of Bettona. - https://www.exploring-umbria.com/en/fortified-villages-in-umbria-rare-hidden-gems/what-to-see-in-bettona/tomba-etrusca/

name: Tumulus of Poggio Gaiella, Chiusi
desc: The Tumulus of Poggio Gaiella (5th century BC), the largest in Etruria, is considered the tomb of King Porsenna, who besieged Rome in 506 BC. The tombs are arranged on several levels, with corridors forming a real labyrinth. - https://www.etruschi.name/chiusi/poggio_gaiella_it.html

name: Tomb of the Grand Duke, Chiusi
desc: The "Tomba del Granduca" (2nd century BC) consists of a single chamber made of travertine blocks. Seven cinerary urns bearing the name of the Pulfna Peris family are placed on the benches. - https://www.loquis.com/en/loquis/565692/Grand+Duke+s+Tomb

name: Tomb of the Monkey, Chiusi
desc: The "Tomba della Scimmia" (c. 475 BC) has three chambers opening onto a central space. Its name comes from a frieze decorated with a monkey in the central chamber of the tomb. It features numerous frescoes (closed to visitors). - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/the-tomb-of-the-monkey-in-the-necropolis-of-poggio-renzo/

name: tomb of Casuccini Pass, Chiusi
desc: The "Tomba del Colle Casuccini" (6th century BC) has three chambers, plus two smaller rooms intended for cinerary urns. It is adorned with abundant frescoes. - https://aroundus.com/p/11673917-tomba-del-colle-casuccini

name: Tomb of the Lion, Chiusi
desc: The "Tomba del Leone" (5th-2nd century BC) is located, along with two other tombs, beneath a tumulus. It contains three main chambers around a central space. The frescoes (including those of the lion) have now disappeared. - https://www.loquis.com/en/loquis/565086/Tomb+of+the+Lion

name: Tomb of the Pilgrim, Chiusi
desc: The "Tomba della Pellegrina" (4th-3rd century BC) is located beneath a tumulus. It contains three main chambers. It contains five sarcophagi and urns. - https://www.archeomedia.net/michele-zazzi-la-tomba-della-pellegrina-dei-sentinate-a-chiusi-si/

name: Tomb of the Chariot, Populonia
desc: (Photo © C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain). The Tomb of the Chariot (7th century BC) has a tumulus 28 meters in diameter, the largest on the site. Two wheels and bronze ornaments, as well as an ivory horn, were found there. San Cerbone Necropolis.

name: Tomb of the Attic Cups, Populonia
desc: San Cerbone Necropolis - https://www.etruschi.name/populonia/necropoli_san_cerbone_it.html

name: Tomb of the Colatoi, Populonia
desc: San Cerbone Necropolis - https://www.etruschi.name/populonia/necropoli_san_cerbone_it.html

name: Tomb of the offering bronze
desc: San Cerbone Necropolis - https://www.etruschi.name/populonia/necropoli_san_cerbone_it.html

name: Tomb of the Burial Beds, Populonia
desc: San Cerbone Necropolis - https://www.etruschi.name/populonia/necropoli_san_cerbone_it.html

name: Tomb of the Amber Beads, Populonia
desc: Necropolis of the Via del Ferro (Iron Road Necropolis)

name: Tomb of the Hescanas, Porano
desc: The tomb, carved into a small wooded hill, belonged to the aristocratic Hescanas family, dating from the late 4th century BC. It is one of the few painted tombs in the Orvieto region (along with the two Golini tombs). It notably depicts a representation of the funeral banquet celebrated in the presence of the dead. - https://www.umbriatourism.it/en/-/tomba-degli-hescanas-en

name: Hildebrand Tomb, Sovana
desc: This famous Hellenistic funerary monument, the Tomba Ildebranda (3rd-2nd century BC), is entirely carved from tufa. Placed on a base overlooking the valley, it comprises a monumental façade hewn on three sides and two lateral staircases. Only traces remain of the polychrome stucco typical of Etruscan decorative art. A long corridor provides access to the tomb. The chamber, in the shape of a Greek cross, contains only a funerary bench. - https://www.visittuscany.com/en/attractions/tomba-ildebranda/

name: Tomb of the Mermaid, Sovana
desc: The "Tomba della Sirena" (3rd-2nd century BC), also known as "the Fountain," in the Sopraripa necropolis, is deeply carved into the tufa rock, with a facade featuring a false door and a decorated pediment. Above the false door is the recumbent effigy of the deceased, flanked by a demon. A narrow access corridor leads to a small chamber, likely a single chamber dedicated to "Vel Nulina, son of Vel," as indicated by an inscription. - https://maremmap.org/ITEM/sorano-sovana-tomba-della-sirena.html#

name: Tomb of the Typhon, Sovana
desc: Located in the Poggio Stanziale necropolis, the "Tomba del Tifone" (4th century BC) is a typical example of a temple-like tomb carved into the tufa. Only traces of the polychrome frescoes remain. To the right, a steep staircase leads to the top of the monument, which bears an altar (cippus). - https://maremmap.org/ITEM/sorano-sovana-tomba-del-tifone.html#

name: Tomb of the Winged Demon, Sovana
desc: The "Tomba dei Demoni Alati" (late 3rd century BC), discovered in 2004, has been methodically restored to its original appearance. It features a façade with a pediment, and the chamber contains a statue of the deceased holding a cup, still bearing its polychrome plaster. Statues of winged demons and lions are also present. - https://maremmap.org/ITEM/sorano-sovana-tomba-dei-demoni-alati.html#

name: Pola Tomb, Sovana
desc: In the Poggio Prisca necropolis, the Pola tomb (3rd century BC), carved entirely from tufa, has a temple-like façade with eight fluted columns (only one of which survives) set on a base, sculpted capitals, and a long corridor (dromos) leading to the cruciform chamber, which contains a funerary bench. - https://maremmap.org/ITEM/sorano-sovana-tomba-pola.html#

name: Tumulus of Poggio Pelliccia, Giuncarico
desc: The tumulus of Poggio Pelliccia (circa 6th century BC) is undoubtedly an aristocratic tomb, as evidenced by the grave goods preserved in the Vetulonia Museum. The earthen mound is surrounded by a dry-stone wall. A long corridor leads to the burial chamber. The vault is formed of concentric stone rings. - https://catalogo.beniculturali.it/detail/ArchaeologicalProperty/0900206527

name: Tomb a dado, Castro
desc: A rock-cut tomb with a dado (cubic) shape, dating to the late 6th century BC, carved into the tufa. It has three chambers, with cornices and sculptures of rams' and lions' heads. - https://archeoquaderni.it/castro-necropoli/

name: Tomb of the Bige, Castro
desc: The "Tomba della Biga" (circa late 6th century BC), a chamber tomb, yielded a complete grave goods set, including a parade chariot (biga) buried with the horses. The chariot is preserved in the National Etruscan Museum of Viterbo. - https://tuttatoscana.net/2025/02/20/la-tomba-della-biga-di-castro/

name: Lattanzi Tomb
desc: A monumental tomb buried in vegetation, decorated with sculpted friezes and lions. Double portico with columns and side steps.

name: Great Tomb, Castel d'Asso
desc: The "Tomba Grande" has three openings. In the large chamber, 14 sarcophagi are present out of the original 40. - https://mindtrip.ai/attraction/viterbo-lazio/big-tomb-rocky-necropolis-castel-dasso/at-LcXTTTDx

name: Tomb of the Urinates Salvies, Castel d'Asso
desc: The tomb of the Urinates Salvies is adjacent to that of the Tetnies. - https://www.etruschi.name/casteldasso/tomba_tetnie_urinates_it.html

name: Orioli Tomb, Castel d'Asso
desc: The burial chamber contained sixty individuals and was used from 250 to 150 BC. - - https://www.italia.it/fr/latium/viterbe/patrimoine-culturel/necropole-etrusque-de-castel-dasso

name: Tomb of the Titnei, Castel d'Asso
desc: Inscriptions and remains of the side ladders. - https://www.italia.it/it/lazio/viterbo/luoghi-della-cultura/necropoli-etrusca-di-castel-dasso

name: Tumulus of Pisciacavallo, Veii
desc: Tumulus tomb, 7th century BC - https://movio.beniculturali.it/mav/galleriadigerhardschwarz/it/50/tumulo-di-pisciacavallo

name: Campana Tomb
desc: The Campana tomb (Tomba Campana), 6th century BC, is a hypogeum tomb decorated with frescoes, now faded. Within the tumulus are two chambers accessible from the dromos." Stone lions guarded the tomb. It had a double-pitched ceiling with funerary benches. - https://www.sotterraneidiroma.it/sites/tomba-campana

name: Tumulus tomb, Veii
desc: Several tumulus tombs surround this one, south of Veii.

name: Tomb of the Ducks, Veii
desc: The Tomb of the Ducks (Tomba delle anatre), from the Orientalizing period (7th century BC), belongs to an Etruscan prince named Larth. It is a single-chamber tomb, frescoed including the ceiling. Five ducks are depicted in a line. - https://www.parchilazio.it/veio-schede-346-tomba_delle_anatre

name: Tomb of the Roaring Lions, Veii
desc: The "Tomba dei Leoni Ruggenti" was discovered in 2006. It is the oldest known painted Etruscan tomb (circa 680 BC). A corridor leads to a square chamber decorated with frescoes (birds and felines). Although looted, ceramics, jewelry, a sword, and a decorated war chariot were found inside. - https://www.parchilazio.it/schede-351-tomba_dei_leoni_ruggenti

name: Torlonia Tomb, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba Torlonia" (4th century BC) has a monumental entrance, with a door flanked by two pillars. A corridor leads to the large burial chamber, which opens onto six side alcoves - https://catalogo.beniculturali.it/detail/ArchaeologicalProperty/1201338986

name: Regolini-Galassi Tomb, Cerveteri
desc: The Regolini-Galassi tomb dates from the Orientalizing period (7th century BC). Discovered intact in 1836, this tumulus tomb is partially carved into the tufa. A short dromos leads to the central antechamber, which has two side cells and another chamber. A deceased woman covered in gold was found there, along with her jewelry, a silver table service (with the inscription "I am from Larthia"), gilded silver and bronze objects, a biconical bronze urn, ceremonial shields, a small bucchero vase engraved with one of the oldest Etruscan alphabets, a wooden chariot, etc. Many of these pieces are kept in the Gregorian Etruscan Museum in the Vatican. - https://fr.aroundus.com/p/11674505-tombe-regolini-galassi

name: Tomb of the Tarquini, Cerveteri
desc: In the "Tomba dei Tarquini," 70 inscribed, engraved, or painted inscriptions were found, showing that eight generations of the Tarquin family were buried there, from the 3rd century BC to 50 BC. The tomb dates back to the 4th century BC, leading to successive transformations during this period. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/tarquini.htm

name: Tomb of the Triclinium, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba del Triclinio" is a hypogeum from the 4th century BC, with a long access corridor. The frescoes have been transferred to a reconstruction of the tomb at the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. They depict banquet scenes where three couples, reclining on klinai (limestone cushions), are entertained by musicians and dancers surrounded by birds and olive trees. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-triclinium/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Sarcophagi, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba dei Sarcofagi" (4th century BC) belonged to the Apucus family. It comprises two sections, built shortly after each other, containing limestone sarcophagi. The decorative paintings have since disappeared. - http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/sarcofagi.htm

name: Alcove Tomb, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba dell'Alcova," a hypogeum, comprises a stepped dromos and a large chamber with a ceiling, false beams, and pilasters defining the alcove (4th-3rd century BC). - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/alcova.htm

name: Tomb of the Five Chairs, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba delle Cinque Sedie" (late 7th century BC) includes a dromos and three chambers. Five sculpted seats with footrests were found along one wall, each bearing a terracotta statue when it was discovered. A terracotta statuette of a seated dignitary was also found there. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/cinque_sedie.htm

name: Tumulus of the Ship, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tumulo della Nave" (7th century BC) contains a single tomb, accessible via a long, open-air dromos. The tomb, which has five chambers, takes its name from the remains of a ship. The left-hand chamber, a replica of a rectangular house, is particularly noteworthy, as it contains a funerary bed. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/nave.htm

name: Moretti Tumulus, Cerveteri
desc: The Moretti tomb is located in a medium-sized tumulus dating from the late 6th century BC. Its layout is unique among those found at Cerveteri: it comprises ten chambers, two on either side of the vestibule, followed by a large central chamber with two columns in the Tuscan style; seven more chambers then follow. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/moretti.htm

name: Tomb of the Painted Animals, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba degli Animali Dipinti" (Tomb of the Painted Animals) is situated within a monumental tumulus containing four chambers (7th century BC), the main one featuring two pairs of columns, a bench, a circular vestibule, and a sarcophagus. The vestibule paintings have since disappeared. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/animali_dipinti.htm

name: Tomb of the Chairs and Shields, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba degli scudi e delle sedie" (Tomb of the Swords and Seats) is a chambered tomb (7th-6th century BC), whose dromos (entrance passage) leads to a chamber, then to three other chambers. Six beds carved from tufa were found there (for men; sarcophagi were intended for women). Fourteen shields are engraved on the walls. It is located in the same tumulus as the Tomba dei Leoni dipinti (Tomb of the Painted Lions) and the Tomba dell'Argilla (Tomb of Clay). This tumulus, with its 40 m diameter, is one of the largest in the necropolis - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/scudi_sedie.htm

name: Tomb of the Capitals, Cerveteri
desc: (Photos ©C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain, and Raoul Kieffer) The Tomb of the Capitals (6th century BC) is carved into the tufa. It owes its name to two columns with capitals supporting the ceiling of the main chamber. It is accessed via a small dromos. Eight two-person funerary benches are present. - - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/capitelli.htm

name: Tomb of the Beds and Sarcophagi, Tumulus 2, Cerveteri
desc:
(Photo ©Raoul Kieffer) The Tomb of the Beds and Sarcophagi (6th century BC) is included in Tumulus 2.
It has two side chambers and two others in the center, which have a gabled ceiling. Stone benches, beds, and sarcophagi are present. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/letti_funebri.htm

name: Tomb of the Greek Vases, Tumulus 2, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba dei Vasi Greci" (6th century BC) is located beneath Tumulus 2, along with the Tomb of the Hut, the Tomb of the Beds, and the Sarcophagi and the Tomb of the Jars and Firedogs. It is accessed via a dromos. The main chamber has a gabled ceiling. There are side benches intended for urns and sarcophagi. Some chambers contain beds. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/vasi_greci.htm

name: Tomb of the Corniche, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tumula della Cornice" has several burial chambers and imitates an Etruscan house. A cornice runs along the walls of the main chamber, which also contains thrones with footrests - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/cornice.htm

name: Tomb of the Casetta, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba della Casetta," dating from the 6th century BC and carved from a layer of tufa, has a small corridor leading to a vestibule, which provides access to a series of chambers. The openings and doors are surmounted by an arch. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/casetta.htm

name: Tomb of the Reliefs, Cerveteri
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer) The large Tomb of the Reliefs (4th century BC) is that of the Matunas family. It comprises 13 burial niches and an additional sculpted projection that could accommodate 34 bodies. Access is via a long dromos leading to a large hall supported by two columns. Stucco bas-reliefs depict various objects. - https://tarquinia-cerveteri.it/en/cerveteri/necropolis-of-cerveteri/tomb-of-the-reliefs/

name: Tomb of Marce Ursus, Cerveteri
desc: The cube-shaped tomb of Marce Ursus has two chambers. Its distinctive feature is two inscriptions carved into the tufa on the chamber walls. One gives the tomb its name, Marce Ursus; the second is incomplete. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/marce_ursus.htm

name: Maroi Tumulus, Cerveteri
desc: The Maroi tumulus was named in honor of Countess Maroi, who financed the excavation. It is one of the largest in Banditaccia. It contains three burial chambers from different periods (7th and 6th centuries BC). The largest tomb has an elliptical vestibule and a flat ceiling with small rafters and the oblique lines of the reeds that covered the roof carved into the tufa. The main burial chamber, at the back of the vestibule, is divided into two parts by two large pillars. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/maroi.htm

name: Mengarelli Tumulus, Cerveteri
desc: A magnificent example of a tomb that replicates an Etruscan aristocratic dwelling, although unfinished, perhaps because the family has disappeared. The diameter of the tumulus exceeds 30 meters for a single tomb. The entrance, 9 meters deep, is followed by two small cells, then a circular antechamber with exposed beams. In the chamber, between the two beds, the beginning of the excavation of a corridor is visible. The last chamber contains two beds on a bench. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/mengarelli.htm

name: Polychrome tumulus, Cerveteri
desc: (photo ©Raoul Kieffer). This name, Polychrome Tumulus (second half of the 6th century BC), derives from its exterior appearance and the materials used in its construction: the horizontal rows alternate blocks of tufa with blocks of light-colored limestone. The interior consists of a single large room with two central pillars. The walls and ceiling still bear traces of the original red stripes decoration. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/policromo.htm

name: Tumulus of the Colonel, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tumulo del Colonnello," one of the largest in the Banditaccia necropolis, is also one of the oldest (7th century BC). Its unusual name comes from the shape of the decoration on the tumulus's drum, flat and rounded, resembling a colonel's insignia. The tomb is accessed via an iron footbridge that spans the deep, 3-meter-wide ditch surrounding the tumulus. Three of its four tombs can be visited. The oldest consists of a simple 3-meter chamber, similar to that of the contemporary Tomb of the Hut. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/colonnello.htm

name: Tomb of the Doric Columns, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba delle Colonne Doriche" (3rd century BC) is characterized by two imposing Doric columns supporting the chamber. These are not integral to the tufa but were salvaged from another building or tomb. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/colonne_doriche.htm

name: Tomb of the Hut, Tumulus 2, Cerveteri
desc: (Photo ©C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain). The Cabane tomb (Tumulus 2) is one of the oldest to imitate Etruscan houses (7th century BC). It comprises a long dromos with two lateral niches, followed by two successive chambers. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/capanna.htm

name: Tomb of the Jars and the Andirons, Tumulus 2, Cerveteri
desc: The Tomb of the Jars (Tomba dei dolii, 6th century BC) is one of the four tombs in Tumulus 2. It owes its name to the containers (of the dolium type) it contains. The Tomba degli Alari (Tomb of the Firedogs) is accessible via the same dromos. Discovered intact, it contained kitchen equipment (containers, spits and tripods, a tableware set, vases) and iron firedogs, as well as jewelry and women's toiletries. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/doli.htm

name: Tomb of the Well, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tomba del pozzo" (3rd century BC) is so named because of the hole dug next to it, the purpose of which is unknown. It contains two chambers with funerary benches. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/tomba_pozzo.htm

name: Tumulus of Painted Tiles, Cerveteri
desc: The "Tumulo della Tegola Dipinta" is located near the Tomb of the Shields and Chairs.

name: Tomb of Arlena di Castro
desc: At Arlena di Castro, in the locality of La Piantata, the Etruscan tomb "Tomba di Arlena di Castro" (late 4th century BC), a single-chamber tomb, contained chests and sarcophagus lids made of local stone. The most striking feature of this tomb is its pictorial decoration, which covers the entire ceiling and part of the walls, painted in black and red. Two circular shields are carved on the back wall. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/arlena/index.htm

name: Tombs of the Inscriptions, of the Dolphins, of the two Atriums, Ponte Rotto
desc: The "Tomba del Iscrizioni" consists of a central atrium leading to six burial chambers. The dromos was closed by a slab bearing a woman's face. The numerous inscriptions relate to families buried up to the 4th century BC. Ceramics from this tomb are preserved in the Vulci Museum, and a large sarcophagus is on display at the Villa Giulia Museum. Nearby are the Tomb of the Dolphin and the Tomb of the Two Atriums (tomba del Delfino, dei Due Atri). - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/vulci/necr_ponterotto/ponte_rotto.htm

name: Tombe des Sarcophages, Ponte Rotto
desc: La "Tomba dei Sarcofagi" dévolue à la famille des Tutes possède un long couloir d'entrée et un vestibule fermé par une porte. Son plan est complexe. Les plafonds des chambres représentent ceux d’une habitation, avec banquettes funéraires. Il reste des traces de fresques. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/vulci/necr_ponterotto/ponte_rotto.htm

name: Tomb of the Bulls, Ponte Rotto
desc: Like the nearby Tomb of the Sarcophagi, the "Tomba dei Tori" has an inverted T-shaped plan and ceilings decorated to imitate reality. It features funerary benches and sarcophagi, often inscribed, one of which was supported by a base adorned with bulls; this sarcophagus is now in the Archaeological Museum of Vulci. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/vulci/necr_ponterotto/ponte_rotto.htm

name: Rotunda, la Polledrara
desc: Near the Cuccumella, there is a small but interesting stone tumulus called "la Rotonda," dating from the Late Republic or the Roman Empire. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/vulci/necr_polledrara/rotonda.htm

name: Tomb of the Mule, Sesto Fiorentino
desc: The "Tomba della Mula" (7th century BC) is a tholos tomb 9 meters in diameter, without a central pillar. It has been used since the 15th century as the wine cellar of the Villa Garbi Pecchioli… - https://www.comune.sesto-fiorentino.fi.it/it/biblioteca/le-tombe-etrusche

name: Tumulus of the Cima di San Giuliano, Barbarano Romano
desc: One of the main tombs in the San Giuliano necropolis is the Tumulo della Cima (or tomba della Cima), 25 meters in diameter (7th century BC). It is recognizable by its stone drum. A long dromos provides access to three main chambers, two side chambers, and several smaller ones. - https://www.etruschi.name/sangiuliano/tumulo_cima_it.html

name: Hypogeum of San Manno, Ferro di Cavallo, Perugia
desc: The "Ipogeo di San Manno" is a hypogeum tomb from the 3rd century BC. It is located in the medieval church of San Manno, which belonged to the Knights of Malta. It is a chamber tomb with a barrel vault constructed of tufa blocks, and two side chambers. It forms part of the church's crypt. At the entrance to the left-hand cell, an Etruscan inscription lists the names of the occupants of the original tomb (the Precu family) - https://www.umbriatourism.it/en/-/san-manno-hypogeum-perugia

name: Hypogeum of Villa Sperandio, Perugia
desc: The "Ipogeo di Villa Sperandio" (2nd century BC) is located within the property of the same name, at a depth of approximately 5 meters. Its sarcophagus and funerary furnishings are on display at the National Archaeological Museum of Perugia. - https://www.umbriatourism.it/en/-/the-villa-dello-sperandio-necropolis

name: Boschetti Tomb, Carmignano
desc: The small "Tomba di Boschetti," of the archaic type, consists only of wall remains, a small discovered dromos, and a small vestibule leading to the burial chamber where, among other things, an ivory pyxis and black- and red-figure vases were found. These are on display at the Archaeological Museum of Artimino.

name: Tomb of the Column, San Lorenzo Nuovo
desc: (Photo © Luigi Catena) Near Grotte di Castro, the Tomb of the Column (5th-4th century BC), carved into the tufa, has a short dromos and a rectangular chamber with funerary benches, a double-pitched ceiling, and a columen in relief. It is supported by a central column. (5th-4th century BC) - https://www.tusciaup.com/la-tomba-della-colonna-di-san-lorenzo-nuovo/125836

name: Tomb of the Archer, Bargino
desc: The "Tomba dell'Arciere" (7th century BC) features a small dromos leading to a single square chamber with a central column. The beams, ceiling, and the stele that was placed at the entrance or atop the tumulus are made of sandstone. A few objects, including ivory, bronze, and gold, were also found. - https://www.visitchianti.net/the-tomb-of-the-archer/?lang=en

name: Tumulus of the Etruscan prince
desc: The "Tumulo del Principe etrusco" (7th century BC) is a tumulus 20 meters in diameter, surrounded by equidistant vertical stone slabs. In the center of a square pit was a wooden box containing the remains of a funerary meal and a few iron objects (trident, knife). Approximately twenty tombs of men and women are arranged around the tumulus. - https://www.turismo.pisa.it/index.php/en/place/tumulus-of-the-etruscan-prince

name: Tumulus of Monte Oliviero
desc: Tumulo di Monte Oliviero - https://movio.beniculturali.it/mav/galleriadigerhardschwarz/nl/30/monte-oliviero

name: Tomb of Torara or Vecchiarelli Tomb, Manziana
desc: The Tomb of the Torara or Tomba Vecchiarelli (6th century BC) comprises a dromos and a central chamber providing access to four other chambers. Four thrones are placed on the sides. The care with which the architectural decoration was made, particularly the doors and the ceiling, suggests that it belonged to a wealthy family. Funerary beds (one in each chamber). Ceramic vases and a ladle were found there. - https://fondoambiente.it/luoghi/tomba-etrusca-della-torara?ldc=

name: Tomb of the Statues, Ceri
desc: In the Fornaci necropolis, near Ceri, a two-chambered tomb (7th century BC) is known for two statues carved in tufa (unfortunately vandalized recently), placed beside the entrance, which are thought to represent demons or seated ancestors watching over the tomb.

name: Tumulus Chigi, Monte Aguzzo
desc: The "tumulo Chigi" is a large, monumental tomb from the 7th century BC belonging to the aristocratic Etruscan Pepuna family. Two vases were found there, now on display at the National Etruscan Museum of Villa Giulia. - https://movio.beniculturali.it/mav/galleriadigerhardschwarz/it/28/monte-aguzzo

name: Tomb of the Augurs, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc:
"Tomba degli Auguri"" (chamber tomb, second half of the 6th century BC). The chamber It simulates a house, with its double-pitched ceiling.
The frescoes depict various figures (a magistrate, wrestlers, an augur or referee of games), figures in prayer with outstretched arms, and mourners. A few animals are also present. In a scene perhaps foreshadowing gladiatorial combat, we see a Phersu: a man, holding a club but with his head covered by a sack, confronts a ferocious dog. The footprints of two funerary couches are visible on the floor. A large doorway is painted in trompe-l'œil with depictions of a funeral ceremony. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-augurs/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Lionesses, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc:
"(Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of the Lionesses (chamber tomb, late 6th century BC) has a small chamber with a double-pitched ceiling decorated in a checkerboard pattern, with six painted Doric columns.
At the far end, there is a niche for the funerary urn. The frescoes are of high quality. The pediment at the back of the chamber depicts two lionesses facing each other, and a dancer accompanied by a cithara and a double flute. A couple in a sensual pose, and men reclining on cushions. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-lionesses/?lang=en"

name: Tomb of the Warrior, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Guerriero" (chamber tomb, late 5th century BC) has a single rectangular chamber with a double-pitched ceiling. A fresco depicts a musician accompanying a warrior's dance. On the back pediment are two roosters and two panthers. The main scene depicts a banquet. On other walls are scenes of games (disco, javelin throwing, boxers), animals, etc. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-warrior/?lang=en

name: Tomb of Hunting and Fishing, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of the Hunt and the Fisherman (chamber tomb, late 6th century BC) comprises two fully painted burial chambers. The first depicts banquet scenes with dancing, wine, and outdoor games. A return from the hunt is shown on the pediment. The second presents a seascape with dolphins, fishermen, a hunter, a diver, and another family banquet scene. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-hunting-and-fishing/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Hunters, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of the Hunters (chamber tomb, late 6th century BC) is unique because the chamber does not depict a house, but a "Hunting Lodge" (Padiglione di Caccia), a tent sheltering hunters. It features numerous hunting scenes with horsemen, dogs, bulls, lions, and deer. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Cacciatore/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Jugglers, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: "Tomba dei Giocolieri" (chamber tomb, second half of the 6th century BC). It contains a small chamber with a double-pitched ceiling forming a pavilion. Below the tympanum, the fresco depicts a red lion and a blue panther. In the background, a man watches jugglers in action, to the sound of a flute. Other figures include spectators, dancers, musicians, etc. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-jugglers/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Leopards, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc:
(Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of the Leopards (chamber tomb, second half of the 5th century BC) features some of the most important and highly detailed Etruscan frescoes. Two symmetrical leopards appear facing the entrance. The ceiling is double-pitched and decorated in a checkerboard pattern.
The frescoes depict a funerary banquet; on the left, musicians (double flute and cithara) accompany dancers. On the right, three married couples whose fresco reveals the clothing of the period. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-leopards/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Festoons, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dei Festoni" (3rd century BC) is a single-chamber hypogeum decorated with festoons. The fresco also depicts three shields and two demons with a large hammer, guarding the door. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Festoni/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Baron, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Barone" (chamber tomb, 6th century BC) has a gabled ceiling with a central beam. The frescoes on the front wall depict a woman and a bearded man holding the arm of a flautist. To the right, two young men hold horses by the bridle. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-baron/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Underworld, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dell'Orco" (Hellenistic tomb, late 4th century BC) contains two large burial chambers. The first depicts a (very deteriorated) scene of a banquet of the Velcha family, and the second features mythological scenes of Greek and Etruscan inspiration, including, as was becoming common at the time, the passage to the afterlife. Mythological figures (Aita, Fersipnei, Celun, Tuchulcha) from the Etruscan pantheon are also depicted. - https://aroundus.com/p/8124812-tomb-of-orcus

name: Tomb of the Shields, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba degli Scudi" (chamber tomb, second half of the 4th century BC) comprises a central chamber with a double-pitched ceiling and ridge beam, and doors and windows providing access to three other chambers. The central chamber contains frescoes showing the aristocratic Velcha family participating in various banquets. The burial chamber at the far end is decorated with inscriptions and large shields. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-shields/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Biges, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The frescoes from the "Tomba delle Bighe" or Stackelberg Tomb (a chamber tomb dating from the 5th century BC) have been detached and transferred to the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. They depict chariot races with two horses (the bigae), banquets, sporting events, and erotic games. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-bigas/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Triclinium , Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain). The frescoes from the Triclinium tomb (hypogeum, 5th century BC) were detached and transferred to the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. They depict banquet scenes with three reclining couples, entertained by musicians and dancers. The men are dressed in Etruscan togas, and the women in tebenna, a cloak and cape. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-triclinium/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Mortuary Bed, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Letto Funebre" (a chamber tomb dating from the 5th century BC) has a rectangular chamber. Its frescoes have also been detached and transferred to the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. The fresco on the back wall depicts a funerary banquet. On the sides are funerary games in honor of the deceased. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Letto%20Funebre/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Ship, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba della Nave" (chamber tomb, 5th century BC) consists of a single rectangular chamber. The frescoes depicted a transport ship on the left wall and, on the right, the classic banquet scene in honor of the deceased, with guests, servants, and musicians. These frescoes were detached and transferred to the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. The sarcophagus was too bulky to be carried off by looters. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-ship/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Fustigation, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of the Flogging (chamber tomb, 5th century BC), with its double-pitched ceiling and central beam, owes its name to two erotic scenes, scenes of dance and music. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-flogging/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Olympiads, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba delle Olimpiadi" (chamber tomb, 6th century BC) has a rectangular chamber with columns. The frescoes depicted sporting events in honor of the deceased (foot races, discus throwing, long jump, boxing, and chariot racing). Also depicted is the Phersu, a masked man who sets a dog on a man with a sack over his head, who tries to defend himself with a club. The frescoes were detached and transferred to the National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-olympic-games/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Bulls, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc:
The ""Tomb of the Tori"""" (6th century BC) comprises a vestibule with columns and two burial chambers. It belonged to the Spurina family, aristocrats of Tarquinia.
The frescoes depict two bulls wearing human-faced masks in front of erotic scenes; Achilles ambushing Troilus, son of Priam; a chimera; and a man riding a hippocampus. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-bulls/?lang=en

name: Tomb of Punchinello, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Pulcinella" (chamber tomb, 6th century BC) includes a chamber with a double-pitched ceiling. A fresco depicts a dancing Phersu on the left wall, whose costume evokes Harlequin and Punchinello. On the back pediment, two lions face each other. On the sides, funerary games (dances, music, sports, and horse races) are shown. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-pulcella/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Maid, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Maid's tomb (chamber tomb, 6th century BC) comprises a rectangular chamber with a niche for a sarcophagus at the back. Scenes of the banquet are depicted on the side walls. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-pulcella/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Charons, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of Charon (3rd century BC) has two chambers, with a fresco depicting two winged demons (Charon) on either side of a doorway, symbolizing the passage to the afterlife. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-charuns/?lang=en

name: Cardarelli Tomb, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc:
(Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Cardarelli Tomb (chamber tomb, late 6th century BC) has a chamber with a gabled and beamed ceiling. The frescoes depict athletes and the Gates of Hell in the center of the back wall, flanked by a musician, and on the pediment, lions attacking a gazelle.
On the left, a man holding a kylix, preceded by a double flute player, advances a richly dressed woman, a slave, and a young girl carrying a mirror.
On the right, a cottabos game, which accompanied banquets, is shown, featuring a man holding two vessels, a dancer, and a musician. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/cardarelli-tomb/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Bacchants, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Bacchantes' Tomb (chamber tomb, late 6th century BC) has a chamber with a gabled and beamed ceiling, painted with flowers. The fresco on the pediment, supported by a column, depicts two felines hunting. Other frescoes with a semi-nude dancer and a crowned female dancer gave the tomb its name. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-bacchants/?lang=en

name: Tomb of Typhon, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Tifone" (hypogeum tomb, 2nd-1st century BC), accessible via a dromos, has a vaulted main chamber with a central pillar, benches, and sarcophagi in other chambers. The frescoes depict rosettes, dolphins, and waves. On the pillar is the monster Typhon with outstretched wings. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Tifone/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Little Flowers, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dei Fiorellini" (hypogeum tomb, second half of the 5th century BC) has a single chamber accessible via a dromos, with a gabled ceiling and a central beam. On the sides of the vault, small red circles alternate with flowers. On the back pediment, two roosters are fighting. A fresco depicts a banquet, with a reclining couple served by two naked boys. On either side, a flute player accompanies dancers. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-little-flowers/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Lotus Flower, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Fiore di Loto" (hypogeum tomb, 6th century BC) has a single chamber accessible via a dromos, with a gabled ceiling and a central beam. The frescoes are badly damaged. The sides are decorated with small four-petaled flowers. On the pediment at the back, on either side of the column, a lion and a panther, separated by an inverted lotus flower, face each other. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-lotus-flower/?lang=en

name: Tomb of Mercareccia, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba della Mercareccia" (chamber tomb, 4th-3rd century BC) comprises two chambers arranged on two levels with separate entrances. The upper chamber depicts the residence of an Etruscan magistrate. Only fragments remain of the frescoes that represented animals or the funeral procession in honor of the deceased in the tomb. The lower chamber is also known as the Guasta Tomb. - http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Mercareccia/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Mouse, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Topolino" (6th century BC) comprises a single rectangular room with a double-pitched ceiling and a red-painted column. Frescoes form a red and black frieze on all the walls, along with a decoration of young trees. A small mouse is painted precariously balanced on a leaf. The gables and pediments are richly decorated with figures, guests, and servants. On the left, an erotic motif: a bird with its wings, tail, and talons. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Topolino/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Red Lions, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dei Leoni Rossi" (hypogeum tomb, 6th century BC) comprises a single rectangular chamber with a beam. On the tympanum, two red lions lie facing each other. The column is painted red. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Leoni%20Rossi/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Rooster, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Gallo" (late 5th century BC) consists of a chamber with a gabled ceiling and a funerary niche carved into the left wall. The frescoes depict two roosters on the entrance tympanum and traces of a panther on the rear tympanum. There are also banquet scenes with dancing and music. On the left wall, a masked dancer and a dancer brandishing castanets are shown. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Gallo/index.htm

name: Giglioli Tomb, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba Giglioli" (hypogeum tomb, 4th century BC) is one of the most recent in Tarquinia. The painted decoration depicts weapons hanging from nails, breastplates, a trumpet, and a round shield. Along the side walls are three pseudo-sarcophagi of the Pinies family, on which painted markings remain. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Giglioli/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Stag Hunt, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba della Caccia al Cervo" (5th century BC) consists of a single chamber with a gabled ceiling. The frescoes on the tympanum depict a deer hunt with a dog. The main scene is a banquet, with three reclining couples. The right wall is decorated with dancing. On the left, a faded figure, perhaps the dance of an armed warrior. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-deer-hunt/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Inscriptions, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba delle Iscrizioni" (late 6th century BC) has a single chamber with three false doors. Of the frescoes, only the drawings made during the discovery remain: scenes of sport (boxing, wrestling, and a horse race), a procession of dancers, and scenes of Bacchanalia (an initiation banquet?). On the tympana, lions are depicted hunting deer and satyrs. Numerous inscriptions accompany the paintings. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Iscrizioni/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Master of the Olympiads, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Maestro delle Olimpiadi" (chamber tomb, late 6th century BC) consists of a single chamber with a double-pitched ceiling decorated with red flowers. The frescoes along the walls appear to be purely decorative. They depict horses, riders, and naked runners. In the semi-tympana, to the right and left, a red lion with an azure mane devours a deer. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Maestro%20Olimpiadi/index.htm

name: Built Tomb, la Polledrara
desc: The "Tomba Costruita" (7th century BC), instead of being carved into the rock, is constructed of large blocks, with an entrance for each of the three chambers. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/vulci/necr_polledrara/tomba_costruita.htm

name: Tomb of the Blue Demons, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri" (4th century BC) is decorated with demonic figures with dark skin. blue, surrounded by serpents and demons equipped with oars that transport the deceased beyond the Acheron. Charun was not just a ferryman, but the most famous of the demons. He is armed with a heavy hammer. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-blue-demons/?lang=en

name: Tomb 808, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The frescoes of "Tomba 808" (4th century BC) are badly damaged, except for the back pediment, where two figures and a pillar surmounted by a large, patera-shaped container can be discerned. On the left wall, a kline (dining couch) is depicted with two diners. On the right, a man carries a pole on his shoulders from which containers are suspended. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/808/index.htm

name: Tomb 3697, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 3697" (early 4th century BC) consists of a single chamber with a double-pitched ceiling, from which dampness has caused most of the plaster to detach from the frescoes. On the back wall, a banquet scene and a few birds on the pediment are still visible. - http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/3697/index.htm

name: Tomb 3242, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 3242", also known as the Mauro Cristofani tomb (mid-4th century BC), consists of a small chamber with a double-pitched ceiling. The back wall features a large niche, and two others open onto the side walls. The frescoes, now very faded, depict a funeral celebration with musicians and dancers. - https://www.loquis.com/en/loquis/2946039/Tomb+Mauro+Cristofani

name: Tomb 939, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 939" (first half of the 6th century BC) has two chambers. The decorations are limited to red, brown, and gray bands, and two lions on the pediment of the main chamber. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/939/index.htm

name: Tomb 994, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 994" (first half of the 5th century BC) shows only small fragments of paint on the back walls and the pediment. It depicted a dancer, a bearded man, and another holding a cup (kylix) in his left hand. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/994/index.htm

name: Tomb 1200, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 1200" (first half of the 5th century BC) consists of a single chamber. The frescoes have crumbled, but on the gable end of the back wall, three couples of diners can still be seen on klinai (dining couches). On the left wall, several figures are depicted, one of whom is carrying a staff. On the right, three chariots are participating in a race. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/1200/index.htm

name: Tomb 1560, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 1560" (first half of the 5th century BC) comprises a main room giving access to three secondary chambers. Only the main chamber is frescoed: on the left wall, young trees and a richly adorned dancer are recognizable; on the back wall are a cithara player and unidentifiable figures. On the pediments, two young men face panthers. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/1560/index.htm

name: Tomb 1646, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 1646" (first half of the 6th century BC) comprises a single chamber with a gabled ceiling and a false beam painted red. On the tympanum of the back wall are two red panthers; on the entrance side, a goose with its body outlined in black. - http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/1646/index.htm

name: Tomb 1822, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 1822" (late 5th century BC) comprises a chamber with a gabled ceiling and a column. The tympanum and column are decorated in red. On the sides are discs originally decorated with roses and ivy leaves. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/1822/index.htm

name: Tomb 1999, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 1999" (late 6th century BC) has a single chamber with a gabled ceiling. The frescoes are badly crumbled. On the back wall, a nude figure spins with raised arms, a flautist plays, a woman's arm leans towards a bearded man, and a nude servant holds a wine jug. On the left wall, a man with legs apart holds a leash, probably for a dog, and a smaller, nude figure carries a bag. To the right, a dancing satyr, a small tree, and perhaps another satyr are depicted. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/1999/index.htm

name: Tomb 2015, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 2015" (early 5th century BC) consists of a single chamber with a gabled ceiling. The poorly preserved frescoes depict a dance in honor of the deceased. - http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/2015/index.htm

name: Tomb 3098, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 3098" (late 6th century BC) consists of a single chamber with a gabled ceiling and no columns. On the back wall, decorated with brown, red, and blue stripes, a lion and a panther are shown fighting. On the front wall, two red lions. On the side walls, a banquet scene where a bearded man can be seen facing the guests. - http://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/3098/index.htm

name: Tomb 5513, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba 5513" (5th century BC) consists of a single chamber with a double-pitched ceiling and a decorated column. A banquet scene is visible on the back wall, and on the sides are dancers and musicians. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/5513/index.htm

name: Tomb 5591, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (photo ©Raoul Kieffer). Tomb 5591, also known as the Tomba Mario Moretti (early 5th century BC), consists of a single chamber with a double-pitched ceiling decorated with small flowers. The tympanum at the back depicts two blue-maned lions facing each other. On the back wall are a flute player, a male figure holding a cup (kylix), and a richly dressed woman. On the side walls, dancers alternate with young trees. - - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/moretti-tomb/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Two Roofs (5636), Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (photos ©Raoul Kieffer). The Tomb of the Two Detti (late 3rd century BC) differs from the previous ones: the ceiling is flat, and the painted area is limited to the right wall and the central pillar. On the latter, we see a winged Charun, and on the wall, a scene where the deceased prepares to cross the threshold of the afterlife, guarded by Charun and Vanth, the demoness brandishing a torch. We also see figures, perhaps relatives who died previously. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-two-roofs/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Anina, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba degli Anina" (late 3rd century BC) belonged to the aristocratic family of the same name, whose founder is believed to be Larth Anina. It consists of a single large, square chamber with a flat ceiling. On either side of the door are painted the two Etruscan demons of death: Charun, depicted with a hammer, punishes souls, while Vanth, the principal demoness, winged and bare-breasted, holds a torch to light the way to the afterlife. This scene clearly places us at the decline of Etruscan civilization, when the subsoil of Tarquinia became populated by demons. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/anina-tomb/?lang=en

name: Bartoccini Tomb, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba Bartoccini" (6th century BC) is an excellent example of house-tombs with their characteristic complex layout. The main chamber, the most richly decorated, provides access to three secondary cells located on a lower level. Frescoes cover the double-pitched ceilings and their columns. The checkerboard pattern dominates the walls. The pediment of the back wall depicts a banquet scene. The one on the entrance wall shows two red seahorses. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/bartoccini-tomb/?lang=en

name: Bertazzoni Tomb, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba Bertazzoni" (late 5th or early 4th century BC) comprises a chamber with a double-pitched ceiling and three large funerary niches carved into the walls. The frescoes are badly damaged and difficult to see. The pediment of the back wall may have depicted a hunting scene with small figures. The side walls of the tomb and the niches (whose ceilings are painted in a checkerboard pattern) depict the usual funerary banquet, with singers and dancers. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Bertazzoni/index.htm

name: Tomb of Frontoncino, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Frontoncino" (6th century BC) only preserves the fresco on the back wall (a banquet scene with three reclining guests), which nevertheless retains remarkably vibrant colors. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Frontoncino/index.htm

name: Francesca Giustiniani Tomb, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba Francesca Giustiniani" (second half of the 5th century BC) features decoration that illustrates the period when Etruscan artists were breaking free from Greek influence. We see a woman playing a double flute, and a richly dressed man and woman dancing before a chariot drawn by winged horses. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Giustiniani/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Jade Lions, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dei Leoni di Giada" (6th century BC) features badly damaged paintings, as well as a fragmentary Doric door with two panels. The pediment is adorned with two emerald-green lions. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Leoni%20di%20Giada/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Panthers, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba delle Pantere" (late 7th century BC), one of the oldest in Tarquinia, is a prime example of an "Orientalizing" hypogeum tomb. It comprises a small, narrow, rectangular chamber with a double-pitched ceiling. The decoration, in red and black, is limited to the back wall. It depicts two panthers in profile, their forepaws resting on the protome of another feline. It is surrounded by other tombs of various types (pit, chamber, well). - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-panthers/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Cardinal, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba del Cardinale" (3rd century BC) comprises a large rectangular room supported by four large central pillars, a flat ceiling with projecting beams on the right side, coffered in the central section, and smooth on the left. Benches line the walls. The frescoes are poorly preserved and known mainly through old drawings. The decoration is concentrated on the pillar capitals (a frieze of rosettes, warriors fighting against a dark background, and a vegetal frieze) and the walls of the right half of the tomb, with a long frieze depicting nearly 200 figures, the deceased's journey to the afterlife, demons, processions, etc. Numerous inscriptions attribute the tomb to the aristocratic Vestarcnia family. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Cardinale/index.htm

name: Querciola Tomb, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba della Querciola" (late 5th century BC) comprises a single rectangular chamber with a double-pitched ceiling. Its frescoes, already badly damaged when discovered, included banquet scenes with dancers and musicians in the upper section, and boar hunt scenes in the lower section. The tympana depicted warriors, horses, and panthers. It is worth noting that another Querciola Tomb existed in the same location, but it is now lost. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Querciola/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Niches, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The "Tomba dei Loculi" (5th-4th century BC) features a chamber with a double-pitched ceiling and false beams, providing access to three large burial niches. The pediment of the back niche is decorated with palmettes and volutes. On the somewhat deteriorated walls, dancers and musicians are depicted in a landscape of red trees. On the back wall, to the right of the niche, a dancing warrior carries a shield and spear. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Loculi/index.htm

name: Queen's Tumulus, Doganaccia (Tarquinia)
desc: The "Tumulo della Regina" (7th century BC) is believed to have been used for one or more very high-ranking families. Excavations have revealed the northern part of the drum. The foundation was hewn into the bedrock. Its diameter reaches 40 meters, making it the largest tumulus in Tarquinia. - https://www.archeomedia.net/tarquinia-vt-il-tumulo-della-regina/

name: King's Tumulus, Doganaccia (Tarquinia)
desc:
The ""Tumulo del Re"" (7th century BC), the first of the princely tumuli of Doganaccia, consists of a single rectangular burial chamber with a pointed arch vault and a large entrance. Its diameter exceeds 35 meters.
Despite looting, ceramics related to banquet practices, some bronze fragments, gold leaf from an ornament, and the iron remains of a chariot have been discovered. - https://archeologiavocidalpassato.com/tag/tumulo-del-re/

name: Twin tombs, Doganaccia (Tarquinia)
desc: Behind the Queen's Tumulus are two twin tombs (Tomba Gemina) dating from the second half of the 7th century BC. The tomb, dating from the 7th-6th century BC, was likely intended for noble couples related to the occupants of the tumulus. It includes a grand staircase, a deep vestibule that contained a chariot, and two adjacent rectangular chambers with funerary benches. The roof was probably of an orientalizing false ogival style.

name: Tomb of the Gorgon, Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: (Photo ©Raoul Kieffer). The Gorgon's Tomb (early 6th century BC) features, on its back pediment, the head of the Gorgon with its tongue protruding. On either side, graceful trees with perched doves. Two figures holding staffs are also depicted greeting each other amidst other trees and blue birds. - https://tarquiniaturismo.com/tomb-of-the-gorgoneion/?lang=en

name: Tomb of the Cylindrical Pyxis, San Cerbone, Populonia
desc: (Photo © C. Bureaux, Lycée de la Plaine de l'Ain). The drum of the Pyxides tumulus tomb (7th century BC), where vessels of this type were found, is surrounded by a cornice. The tumulus has disappeared. San Cerbone Necropolis - https://www.etruschi.name/populonia/necropoli_san_cerbone_it.html.

name: Tomb of the Belvedere, Vetulonia
desc: The "Tomba del Belvedere" (7th-6th century BC) is a tholos tomb with a rectangular chamber, a central pillar, an access dromos, and three niches.

name: Tumulus of the Quarry, Vetulonia
desc:
The ""Tumulo della Pietrera"" (Quarry Tumulus), dating from the 7th century BC, is a tholos tomb covered by a tumulus with a diameter of 60 meters.
It contains two superimposed tombs: one with a dromos, a circular chamber, and two side cells; above it, a rectangular chamber tomb with a vestibule and two side cells. The finds are housed in Florence and the Isidoro Falchi Archaeological Museum in Vetulonia. - https://archeoquaderni.it/vetulonia-tumulo-della-pietrera/

name: Tumulus of Diavolino II, Vetulonia
desc: The "Tumulo del Diavolino II" (7th century BC) is preceded by a long corridor and a rectangular chamber, with a tholos and a central pillar. - https://archeoquaderni.it/vetulonia-tomba-del-diavolino-ii/

name: Tomb of the Painted Lions and Tomb of Clay, Cerveteri
desc:
The ""Tomba dei Leoni Dipinti"" and the ""Tomba dell'Argilla"" are located in the same tumulus ""degli Scudi e delle Sedie,"" which, at 40 meters in diameter, is one of the largest in the necropolis.
The first is a three-chambered tomb dating from the 7th century BC with an Orientalizing-style dromos. The ceiling of the central chamber features a structure of concentric circles. It contains beds and a bench. The frescoes of lions are now faded.
The second is a chambered tomb from the 6th-5th centuries BC, which was decorated with frescoes depicting dancers, jugglers, horses, and centaurs. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/etruschi_tuscia/cerveteri/leoni_dipinti.htm

name: Bruschi Tomb, Tarquinia
desc: The Bruschi tomb (5th century BC), discovered outside the Monterozzi necropolis, near the Calvario necropolis, was already badly damaged when it was discovered in 1864. However, it allowed for the deciphering of the numerous inscriptions and the copying of what remained of the frescoes. These frescoes, removed and restored, are now on display at the Museo Nazionale Tarquiniense. They depict a procession of magistrates accompanying the deceased, Vel Apnas, into the afterlife, where they meet another procession, probably that of the deceased's ancestors. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Bruschi/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Painted Vases, Tarquinia (Monterozzi
desc: The Tomb of the Painted Vases (late 6th century BC) is decorated with frescoes depicting the classic theme of banquet scenes with dancers. A small table holds three large vessels, two of which are painted. On a kline (banquet couch), a couple is shown, the man affectionately caressing his wife's face. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Vasi%20Dipinti/index.htm

name: Tomb of the Biclinium , Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
desc: The Biclinium tomb (4th century BC) consists of a single chamber. Its paintings are known only from drawings (a banquet scene) made at the time of its discovery in the 18th century.. - https://www.canino.info/inserti/monografie/etruschi/tombe_tarquinia/Biclinio/index.htm
